verses.name: Matthew 11:25
verses.text: At that same time Jesus uttered the words: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that, though you have hidden these things from the wise and learned, you have revealed them to the child-like!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 11:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Yes, Father, I thank you that this has seemed good to you.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 11:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Everything has been committed to me by my Father; nor does anyone fully know the Son, except the Father, or fully know the Father, except the Son and those to whom the Son may choose to reveal him.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 11:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Come to me, all you who toil and are burdened, and I will give you rest!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 11:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Take my yoke on you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble, and ‘you will find rest for your souls’;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 11:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.” </q>  <div eID="gen6937" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.11"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:1
verses.text: About the same time Jesus walked through the cornfields one Sabbath. His disciples were hungry, and began to pick some ears of wheat and eat them.

verses.name: Matthew 12:2
verses.text: But, when the Pharisees saw this, they said: “Look! Your disciples are doing what it is not allowable to do on a Sabbath!”  <div eID="gen6938" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv206"/><div sID="gen6939" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv206"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Have not you read,” </q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“what David did, when he and his companions were hungry — </q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">how he went into the house of God, and how they ate the consecrated bread, through it was not allowable for him or his companions to eat it, but only for the priests?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And have not you read in the law that, on the Sabbath, the priest in the Temple break the Sabbath and yet are not guilty?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Here, however, I tell you, there is something greater than the Temple!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Had you learned the meaning of the words — ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned those who are not guilty.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.” </q>  <div eID="gen6939" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv207"/><div sID="gen6940" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv207"/> Passing on, Jesus went into their synagogue,

verses.name: Matthew 12:10
verses.text: and there he saw a man with a withered hand. Some people asked Jesus whether it was allowable to work a cure on the Sabbath — so that they might have a charge to bring against him.

verses.name: Matthew 12:11
verses.text: But Jesus said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Which of you, if he had only one sheep, and that sheep fell into a pit on the Sabbath, would not lay hold of it and pull it out?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">How much more precious a person is than a sheep! Therefore it is allowable to do good on the Sabbath.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:13
verses.text: Then he said to the man. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Stretch out your hand.” </q>The man stretched it out; and it had become as sound as the other.

verses.name: Matthew 12:14
verses.text: On coming out, the Pharisees plotted against Jesus, to put him to death.  <div eID="gen6940" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv208"/><div sID="gen6941" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv208"/> Jesus, however, became aware of it, and went away from that place. A number of people followed him, and he cured them all;

verses.name: Matthew 12:16
verses.text: but he warned them not to make him known,

verses.name: Matthew 12:17
verses.text: in fulfillment of these words in the prophet Isaiah —

verses.name: Matthew 12:18
verses.text: ‘Here is my chosen servant, who I love and who pleases me! I will breathe my spirit on him, and he will announce a time of judgment to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Matthew 12:19
verses.text: He will not contend, nor cry aloud, Neither will anyone hear his voice in the streets;

verses.name: Matthew 12:20
verses.text: a bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not quench, until he has brought the judgment to a victorious issue,

verses.name: Matthew 12:21
verses.text: and on his name will the Gentiles rest their hopes.”  <div eID="gen6941" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv209"/><div sID="gen6942" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv209"/> Then some people brought to Jesus a possessed man, who was blind and dumb; and he cured him, so that the man who had been dumb both talked and saw.

verses.name: Matthew 12:23
verses.text: At this all the people were astounded. “Is it possible that this is the son of David?” they exclaimed.

verses.name: Matthew 12:24
verses.text: But the Pharisees heard of it and said: “He drives out demons only by the help of Beelzebul the chief of the demons.”

verses.name: Matthew 12:25
verses.text: Jesus, however, was aware of what was passing in their minds, and said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Any kingdom divided against itself becomes a desolation, and any town or household divided against itself will not last.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So, if Satan drives Satan out, he must be divided against himself; and how, then, can his kingdom last?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And, if it is by Beelzebul’s help that I drive out demons, by whose help is it that your own sons drive them out? Therefore they will themselves be your judges.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But, if it is by the help of the Spirit of God that I drive out demons, then the kingdom of God must already be upon you.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">How, again, can anyone get into a strong man’s house and carry off his goods, without first securing him? Not until then will he plunder his house.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Anyone who is not with me is against me, and the person who does not help me to gather is scattering.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:31
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore, I tell you, people will be forgiven every sin and slander; but slander against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:32
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Whoever speaks against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in the present age, or in the age to come.</q>  <div eID="gen6942" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv210"/><div sID="gen6943" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv210"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">You must assume either that both tree and fruit are good, or that both tree and fruit are worthless; since it is by its fruits that a tree is known.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:34
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">You children of snakes! How can you, evil as you are, say anything good? For what fills the heart will rise to the lips.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:35
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">A good person, from his good stores, produces good things; while an evil person, from his evil stores, produces evil things.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:36
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I tell you that for every careless thing that people say, they must answer on the ‘day of judgment.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:37
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For it is by your words that you will be acquitted, and by your words that you will be condemned.” </q>  <div eID="gen6943" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv211"/><div sID="gen6944" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv211"/> At this point, some teachers of the law and Pharisees spoke up. “Teacher,” they said, “we want to see some sign from you.”  <div eID="gen6944" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv212"/><div sID="gen6945" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv212"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“It is a wicked and unfaithful generation,” </q>answered Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“that is asking for a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:40
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For, just as ‘Jonah was inside the sea-monster three days and three nights,’ so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:41
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">At the judgment, the people of Nineveh will stand up with this generation, and will condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s proclamation; and here is more than a Jonah!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:42
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">At the judgment the Queen of the South will rise up with the present generation, and will condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to listen to the wisdom of Solomon; and here is more than a Solomon!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:43
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">No sooner does a foul spirit leave a person, than it passes through places where there is no water, in search of rest, and does not find it.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:44
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then it says ‘I will go back to the home which I left’; but, on coming there, it finds it unoccupied, and swept, and put in order.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:45
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in, and make their home there; and the last state of that man proves to be worse than the first. So, too, will it be with this wicked generation.” </q>  <div eID="gen6945" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 12:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv213"/><div sID="gen6946" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv213"/> While he was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers were standing outside, asking to speak to him.

verses.name: Matthew 12:47
verses.text: Someone told him this, and Jesus replied:

verses.name: Matthew 12:48
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Who is my mother? And who are my brothers?” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:49
verses.text: Then, stretching out his hands towards his disciples, he said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Here are my mother and my brothers!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 12:50
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For anyone who does the will of my Father who is in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.” </q>  <div eID="gen6946" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv214"/><div sID="gen6947" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen6947" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.12"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:1
verses.text: That same day, when Jesus had left the house and was sitting by the Sea,

verses.name: Matthew 13:2
verses.text: such great crowds gathered around him, that he got into a boat, and sat in it, while all the people stood on the beach.

verses.name: Matthew 13:3
verses.text: Then he told them many truths in parables. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The sower,” </q>he began, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“went out to sow; and,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">as they were sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Some fell on rocky places, where it had not much soil, and, because the soil wasn't deep, sprang up at once.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">As soon as the sun had risen, it was scorched, and, because their roots were not deep enough, withered away.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Some, again, fell into the brambles; but the brambles shot up and choked it.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Some, however, fell on good soil, and yielded a return, sometimes one hundred, sometimes sixty, sometimes thirty fold.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Let those who have ears hear.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv214"/><div sID="gen6948" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv214"/> Afterwards his disciples came to him, and said: “Why do you speak to them in parables?”  <div eID="gen6948" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv215"/><div sID="gen6949" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv215"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“To you,” </q>answered Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“the knowledge of the hidden truths of the kingdom of heaven has been imparted, but not to those.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For, to all who have, more will be given, and they will have abundance; but, from all who have nothing, even what they have will be taken away.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:13
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">That is why I speak to them in parables, because, though they have eyes, they do not see, and though they have ears, they do not hear or understand.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:14
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">In them is being fulfilled that prophecy of Isaiah which says — <lg sID="gen6950"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6951"/>‘You will hear with your ears without ever understanding,<l eID="gen6951" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen6952"/>and, though you have eyes, you will see without ever perceiving,</q><l eID="gen6952" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6953"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:15
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for the mind of this nation has grown dense,<l eID="gen6953" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen6954"/>and their ears are dull of hearing,<l eID="gen6954" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen6955"/>their eyes also have they closed;<l eID="gen6955" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6956"/>Otherwise some day they might perceive with their eyes,<l eID="gen6956" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen6957"/>and with their ears they might hear,<l eID="gen6957" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen6958"/>and in their mind they might understand,<l eID="gen6958" level="2"/> <l level="2" sID="gen6959"/>and might turn —<l eID="gen6959" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen6960"/>and I might heal them.’</q><l eID="gen6960" level="1"/> <lg eID="gen6950"/> <lb/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:16
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:17
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for I tell you that many prophets and good people have longed for the sight of the things which you are seeing, yet never saw them, and to hear the things which you are hearing, yet never heard them.</q>  <div eID="gen6949" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv216"/><div sID="gen6961" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv216"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">Listen, then, yourselves to the parable of the sower.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When anyone hears the message of the kingdom without understanding it, the evil one comes and snatches away what has been sown in their mind. This is the person meant by the seed which was sown along the path.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:20
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">By the seed which was sown on rocky places is meant the person who hears the message, and at once accepts it joyfully;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:21
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">but, as they have no root, they stand for only a short time; and, when trouble or persecution arises because of the message, they fall away at once.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:22
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">By the seed which was sown among the brambles is meant the person who hears the message, but the cares of life and the glamour of wealth completely choke the message, so that it gives no return.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:23
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But by the seed which was sown on the good ground is meant the person who hears the message and understands it, and really yields a return, sometimes one hundred, sometimes sixty, sometimes thirty fold.” </q>  <div eID="gen6961" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv217"/><div sID="gen6962" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv217"/> Another parable which Jesus told them was this — <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The kingdom of heaven is compared to a person who sowed good seed in their field.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But, while everyone was asleep, their enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and then went away.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So, when the blades of corn shot up, and came into ear, the weeds made their appearance also.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The owner’s servants came to them, and said ‘Was not it good seed that you sowed in your field? Where, then, do the weeds in it come from?’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘An enemy has done this,’ was the owner’s answer. ‘Do you wish us, then,’ they asked,’ to go and gather them together?’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘No,’ said he, ‘because while you are pulling up the weeds you might uproot the wheat with them.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Let both grow side by side until harvest; and then I will say to the reapers, Gather the weeds together first, and tie them in bundles for burning; but bring all the wheat into my barn.’” </q>  <div eID="gen6962" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv218"/><div sID="gen6963" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv218"/> Another parable which he told them was this — <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a person took and sowed in his field.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:32
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">This seed is smaller than all other seeds, but, when it has grown up, it is larger than the herbs and becomes a tree, so that ‘the wild birds come and roost in its branches.’” </q>  <div eID="gen6963" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv219"/><div sID="gen6964" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv219"/> This was another parable which Jesus related — <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The kingdom of heaven is like some yeast which a woman took and covered up in three pecks of flour, until the whole had risen.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:34
verses.text: Of all this Jesus spoke to the crowd in parables; indeed to them he used never to speak at all except in parables,

verses.name: Matthew 13:35
verses.text: in fulfillment of these words in the prophet — ‘I will speak to them in parables; I will utter things kept secret since the foundation of the world.’  <div eID="gen6964" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv220"/><div sID="gen6965" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv220"/> Then Jesus left the crowd, and went into the house. Presently his disciples came to him, and said: “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”

verses.name: Matthew 13:37
verses.text: He answered: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The sower of the good seed is the Son of Man.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:38
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The field is the world. By the good seed is meant the people of the kingdom. The weeds are the wicked,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:39
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and the enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest time is the close of the age, and the reapers are angels.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:40
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And, just as the weeds are gathered and burnt, so it will be at the close of the age.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:41
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather from his kingdom all that hinders and those who live in sin,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:42
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and ‘will throw them into the blazing furnace,’ where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:43
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then will the righteous shine, like the sun, in the kingdom of their Father. Let him who has ears hear.</q>  <div eID="gen6965" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:44
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv221"/><div sID="gen6966" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv221"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field, which a person found and hid again, and then, in their delight, went and sold everything that they had, and bought that field.</q>  <div eID="gen6966" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv222"/><div sID="gen6967" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv222"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of choice pearls.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:46
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Finding one of great value, they went and sold everything that they had, and bought it.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:47
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Or again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net which was cast into the sea, and caught fish of all kinds.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:48
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When it was full, they hauled it up on the beach, and sat down and sorted the good fish into baskets, but threw the worthless ones away.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:49
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So will it be at the close of the age. The angels will go out and separate the wicked from the righteous,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:50
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and ‘will throw them into the blazing furnace,’ where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.</q>  <div eID="gen6967" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:51
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv223"/><div sID="gen6968" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv223"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">Have you understood all this?” </q>Jesus asked. “Yes,” they answered.

verses.name: Matthew 13:52
verses.text: Then he added: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“So every teacher of the law, who has received instruction about the kingdom of heaven, is like a householder who produces from his stores things both new and old.” </q>  <div eID="gen6968" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 13:53
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv224"/><div sID="gen6969" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv224"/> When Jesus had finished these parables, he withdrew from that place.

verses.name: Matthew 13:54
verses.text: Going to his own part of the country, he taught the people in their synagogue in such a manner that they were deeply impressed. “Where did he get this wisdom?” they said, “and the miracles?

verses.name: Matthew 13:55
verses.text: Is not he the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, and Joseph, and Simon, and Judas?

verses.name: Matthew 13:56
verses.text: And his sisters, too — are not they all living among us? Where, then did he get all this?”

verses.name: Matthew 13:57
verses.text: These things proved a hindrance to their believing in him. But Jesus said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country and in his own house.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 13:58
verses.text: He did not work many miracles there, because of their want of faith.  <div eID="gen6969" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv225"/><div sID="gen6970" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen6970" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.13"/>

verses.name: Matthew 14:1
verses.text: At that time Prince Herod heard of the fame of Jesus,

verses.name: Matthew 14:2
verses.text: and said to his attendants: “This must be John the Baptist; he must be risen from the dead, and that is why these miraculous powers are active in him.”

verses.name: Matthew 14:3
verses.text: For Herod had arrested John, put him in chains, and shut him up in prison, to please Herodias, the wife of Herod’s brother Philip.

verses.name: Matthew 14:4
verses.text: For John had said to him ‘You have no right to be living with her.’

verses.name: Matthew 14:5
verses.text: Yet, though Herod wanted to put him to death, he was afraid of the people, because they looked on John as a prophet.

verses.name: Matthew 14:6
verses.text: But, when Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced before his guests, and so pleased Herod,

verses.name: Matthew 14:7
verses.text: that he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked.

verses.name: Matthew 14:8
verses.text: Prompted by her mother, the girl said ‘Give me here, on a dish, the head of John the Baptist.’

verses.name: Matthew 14:9
verses.text: The king was distressed at this; yet, because of his oath and of the guests at his table, he ordered it to be given her.

verses.name: Matthew 14:10
verses.text: He sent and beheaded John in the prison;

verses.name: Matthew 14:11
verses.text: and his head was brought on a dish and given to the girl, and she took it to her mother.

verses.name: Matthew 14:12
verses.text: Then John’s disciples came, and took the body away, and buried it; and went and told Jesus.

verses.name: Matthew 14:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv225"/><div sID="gen6971" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv225"/> When Jesus heard of it, he left privately in a boat to a lonely spot. The people, however, heard of his going, and followed him in crowds from the towns on foot.

verses.name: Matthew 14:14
verses.text: On getting out of the boat, Jesus saw a great crowd, and his heart was moved at the sight of them; and he cured all the sick among them.

verses.name: Matthew 14:15
verses.text: In the evening the disciples came up to him, and said: “This is a lonely spot, and the day is now far advanced; send the crowds away so that they can to the villages, and buy themselves food.”

verses.name: Matthew 14:16
verses.text: But Jesus said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“They need not go away, it is for you to give them something to eat.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 14:17
verses.text: “We have nothing here,” they said, “except five loaves and two fishes.”  <div eID="gen6971" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 14:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv226"/><div sID="gen6972" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv226"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Bring them here to me,” </q>was his reply.

verses.name: Matthew 14:19
verses.text: Jesus ordered the people to take their seats on the grass; and, taking the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and said the blessing, and, after he had broken the loaves, gave them to his disciples; and they gave them to the crowds.

verses.name: Matthew 14:20
verses.text: Everyone had sufficient to eat, and they picked up enough of the broken pieces that were left to fill twelve baskets.

verses.name: Matthew 14:21
verses.text: The men who ate were about five thousand in number, without counting women and children.

verses.name: Matthew 14:22
verses.text: Immediately afterwards Jesus made the disciples get into a boat and cross over in advance of him, while he dismissed the crowds.

verses.name: Matthew 14:23
verses.text: After dismissing the crowds, he went up the hill by himself to pray; and, when evening fell, he was there alone.

verses.name: Matthew 14:24
verses.text: The boat was by this time some miles from shore, laboring in the waves, for the wind was against her.

verses.name: Matthew 14:25
verses.text: Three hours after midnight, however, Jesus came towards the disciples, walking on the water.

verses.name: Matthew 14:26
verses.text: But, when they saw him walking on the water, they were terrified. “It is a ghost,” they exclaimed, and cried out in fear.

verses.name: Matthew 14:27
verses.text: But Jesus at once spoke to them. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Courage!” </q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“It is I; do not be afraid!” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 14:28
verses.text: “Master,” Peter exclaimed, “if it is you, tell me to come to you on the water.”

verses.name: Matthew 14:29
verses.text: Jesus said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Come.” </q>So Peter got down from the boat, and walked on the water, and went towards Jesus;

verses.name: Matthew 14:30
verses.text: but, when he felt the wind, he was frightened, and, beginning to sink, cried out: “Master! Save me!”

verses.name: Matthew 14:31
verses.text: Instantly Jesus stretched out his hand, and caught hold of him. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“You of little faith!” </q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Why did you falter?” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 14:32
verses.text: When they had got into the boat, the wind dropped.

verses.name: Matthew 14:33
verses.text: But the men in the boat threw themselves on their faces before him, and said: “You are indeed God’s Son.”  <div eID="gen6972" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 14:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv227"/><div sID="gen6973" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv227"/> When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret.

verses.name: Matthew 14:35
verses.text: But the people of that place, recognizing Jesus, sent out to the whole country around, and brought to him all who were ill,

verses.name: Matthew 14:36
verses.text: begging him merely to let them touch the tassel of his cloak; and all who touched were made perfectly well.  <div eID="gen6973" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv228"/><div sID="gen6974" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen6974" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.14"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:1
verses.text: Then some Pharisees and teachers of the law came to Jesus, and said:

verses.name: Matthew 15:2
verses.text: “How is it that your disciples break the traditions of our ancestors? For they do not wash their hands when they eat food.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:3
verses.text: His reply was: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“How is it that you on your side break God’s commandments out of respect for your own traditions?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For God said — ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and ‘Let him who abuses his father or mother suffer death,’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">but you say ‘Whenever anyone says to his father or mother “Whatever of mine might have been of service to you is ‘Given to God,’” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">he is in no way bound to honor his father.’ In this way you have nullified the words of God for the sake of your traditions.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Hypocrites! It was well said by Isaiah when he prophesied about you — </q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘This is a people that honor me with their lips, While their hearts are far removed from me;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">but vainly do they worship me, For they teach but human precepts.’” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:10
verses.text: Then Jesus called the people to him, and said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Listen, and mark my words.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">It is not what enters a person’s mouth that ‘defiles’ them, but what comes out from their mouth — that does defile them!” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:12
verses.text: His disciples came up to him, and said: “Do you know that the Pharisees were shocked on hearing what you said?”

verses.name: Matthew 15:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv228"/><div sID="gen6975" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv228"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Every plant,” </q>Jesus replied, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“that my heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted up.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:14
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Let them be; they are but blind guides; and, if one blind person guides another, both of them will fall into a ditch.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:15
verses.text: Peter spoke up: “Explain this saying to us.”  <div eID="gen6975" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv229"/><div sID="gen6976" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv229"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“What, do even you understand nothing yet?” </q>Jesus exclaimed.

verses.name: Matthew 15:17
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Do not you see that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the stomach, and is afterwards expelled?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:18
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But the things that come out of the mouth proceed from the heart, and it is these that defile a person;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for out of the heart proceed evil thoughts — murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, perjury, slander.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:20
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">These are the things that defile a person; but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a person.” </q>  <div eID="gen6976" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv230"/><div sID="gen6977" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv230"/> On going away from that place, Jesus went to the country around Tyre and Sidon.

verses.name: Matthew 15:22
verses.text: There, a Canaanite woman of that district came out and began calling to Jesus: “Take pity on me, Master, Son of David; my daughter is grievously possessed by a demon.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:23
verses.text: But Jesus did not answer her a word; and his disciples came up and begged him to send her away. “She keeps calling out after us,” they said.

verses.name: Matthew 15:24
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I was not sent,” </q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“to anyone except the lost sheep of Israel.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:25
verses.text: But the woman came, and, bowing to the ground before him, said: “Master, help me.”  <div eID="gen6977" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv231"/><div sID="gen6978" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv231"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“It is not fair,” </q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“to take the children’s food and throw it to dogs.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:27
verses.text: “Yes, Master,” she said, “for even dogs do feed on the scraps that fall from their owners’ table.”  <div eID="gen6978" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv232"/><div sID="gen6979" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv232"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Your faith is great,” </q>was his reply to the woman; <q marker="" who="Jesus">“it will be as you wish!” </q>And her daughter was cured that very hour.  <div eID="gen6979" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv233"/><div sID="gen6980" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv233"/> On leaving that place, Jesus went to the shore of the Sea of Galilee; and then went up the hill, and sat down., you will do what not only what has been done to the fig tree, but, even if you should say to this hill ‘Be lifted up and hurled into the sea!’ it would be done.

verses.name: Matthew 15:30
verses.text: Great crowds of people came to him, bringing with them those who were lame, crippled, blind, or dumb, and many others. They put them down at his feet, and he cured them;

verses.name: Matthew 15:31
verses.text: and the crowds were astonished, when they saw the dumb talking, the cripples made sound, the lame walking about, and the blind with their sight restored; and they praised the God of Israel.

verses.name: Matthew 15:32
verses.text: Afterwards Jesus called his disciples to him, and said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“My heart is moved at the sight of all these people, for they have already been with me three days and they have nothing to eat; and I am unwilling to send them away hungry; they might faint on the way home.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 15:33
verses.text: “Where can we,” his disciples asked, “in a lonely place find enough bread for such a crowd as this?”  <div eID="gen6980" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 15:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv234"/><div sID="gen6981" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv234"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“How many loaves have you?” </q>said Jesus. “Seven,” they answered, “and a few small fish.”

verses.name: Matthew 15:35
verses.text: Telling the crowd to sit down on the ground,

verses.name: Matthew 15:36
verses.text: Jesus took the seven loaves and the fish, and, after saying the thanksgiving, broke them, and gave them to the disciples; and the disciples gave them to the crowds.

verses.name: Matthew 15:37
verses.text: Everyone had sufficient to eat, and they picked up seven baskets full of the broken pieces left.

verses.name: Matthew 15:38
verses.text: The men who ate were four thousand in number without counting women and children.

verses.name: Matthew 15:39
verses.text: Then, after dismissing the crowds, Jesus got into the boat, and went to the neighborhood of Magadan.  <div eID="gen6981" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv235"/><div sID="gen6982" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen6982" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.15"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:1
verses.text: Here the Pharisees and Sadducees came up, and, to test Jesus, requested him to show them some sign from the heavens.

verses.name: Matthew 16:2
verses.text: But Jesus answered: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“In the evening you say ‘It will be fine weather, for the sky is as red as fire.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:3
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But in the morning you say ‘Today it will be stormy, for the sky is as red as fire and threatening.’ You learn to read the sky; yet you are unable to read the signs of the times!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">A wicked and unfaithful generation is asking for a sign, but no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah.” </q>So he left them and went away.

verses.name: Matthew 16:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv235"/><div sID="gen6983" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv235"/> Now the disciples had crossed to the opposite shore, and had forgotten to take any bread.

verses.name: Matthew 16:6
verses.text: Presently Jesus said to them: “Take care and be on your guard against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

verses.name: Matthew 16:7
verses.text: But the disciples began talking among themselves about their having brought no bread.

verses.name: Matthew 16:8
verses.text: On noticing this, Jesus said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Why are you talking among yourselves about your being short of bread, you of little faith?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Do not you yet see, nor remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took away?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:10
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Nor yet the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many basketfuls you took away?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">How is it that you do not see that I was not speaking about bread? Be on your guard against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:12
verses.text: Then they understood that he had told them to be on their guard, not against the leaven of bread, but against the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.  <div eID="gen6983" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv236"/><div sID="gen6984" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv236"/> On coming into the neighborhood of Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asked his disciples this question — <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Who do people say that the Son of Man is?” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:14
verses.text: “Some say John the Baptist,” they answered, “Others, however, say that he is Elijah, while others again say Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.”  <div eID="gen6984" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv237"/><div sID="gen6985" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv237"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“But you,” </q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“who do you say that I am?” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:16
verses.text: To this Simon Peter answered: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”  <div eID="gen6985" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv238"/><div sID="gen6986" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv238"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Blessed are you, Simon, Son of Jonah,” </q>Jesus replied. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“For no human being has revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:18
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Yes, and I say to you, Your name is ‘Peter — a Rock, and on this rock I will build my church, and the powers of the place of death will not prevail over it.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you forbid on earth will be held in heaven to be forbidden, and whatever you allow on earth will be held in heaven to be allowed.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:20
verses.text: Then he charged his disciples not to tell anyone that he was the Christ.  <div eID="gen6986" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 16:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv239"/><div sID="gen6987" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv239"/> At that time Jesus Christ began to explain to his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem, and undergo much suffering at the hands of the councillors, and chief priests, and teachers of the law, and be put to death, and rise on the third day.

verses.name: Matthew 16:22
verses.text: But Peter took Jesus aside, and began to rebuke him. “Master,” he said, “please God that will never be your fate!”

verses.name: Matthew 16:23
verses.text: Jesus, however, turning to Peter, said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Out of my way, Satan! You are a hindrance to me; for you look at things, not as God does, but as person does.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:24
verses.text: Then Jesus said to his disciples: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“If anyone wishes to walk in my steps, let him renounce self, and take up his cross, and follow me.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it, and whoever, for my sake, loses his life will find it.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">What good will it do a person to gain the whole world, if he forfeits his life? Or what will a person give that is of equal value with his life?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For the Son of Man is to come in his Father’s glory, with his angels, and then he ‘will give to everyone what his actions deserve.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 16:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I tell you, some of those who are standing here will not know death until they have seen the Son of Man coming into his kingdom.” </q>  <div eID="gen6987" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv240"/><div sID="gen6988" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen6988" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.16"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:1
verses.text: Six days later, Jesus took with him Peter, and the brothers James and John, and led them up a high mountain alone.

verses.name: Matthew 17:2
verses.text: There his appearance was transformed before their eyes; his face shown like the sun, and his clothes became as white as the light.

verses.name: Matthew 17:3
verses.text: All at once Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with Jesus.

verses.name: Matthew 17:4
verses.text: “Master,” exclaimed Peter, interposing, “it is good to be here; if you wish, I will make three tents here, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

verses.name: Matthew 17:5
verses.text: While he was still speaking, a bright cloud enveloped them, and there was a voice from the cloud that said — “This is my dearly loved son, who brings me great joy; listen to him.”

verses.name: Matthew 17:6
verses.text: The disciples, on hearing this, fell on their faces, greatly afraid.

verses.name: Matthew 17:7
verses.text: But Jesus came and touched them, saying as he did so: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Rise up, and do not be afraid.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 17:8
verses.text: When they raised their eyes, they saw no one but Jesus himself alone.

verses.name: Matthew 17:9
verses.text: As they were going down the mountain side, Jesus gave them this warning — <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Do not speak of this vision to anyone, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 17:10
verses.text: “How is it,” his disciples asked, “that our teachers of the law say that Elijah has to come first?”

verses.name: Matthew 17:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv240"/><div sID="gen6989" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv240"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Elijah indeed does come,” </q>Jesus replied, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“and will restore everything;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 17:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and I tell you that Elijah has already come, and people have not recognized him, but have treated him just as they pleased. In the same way, too, the Son of Man is destined to undergo suffering at people’s hands.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 17:13
verses.text: Then the disciples understood that it was of John the Baptist that he had spoken to them.  <div eID="gen6989" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv241"/><div sID="gen6990" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv241"/> When they came to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus, and, kneeling down before him, said:

verses.name: Matthew 17:15
verses.text: “Master, take pity on my son, for he is epileptic and suffers terribly; indeed, he often falls into the fire and into the water;

verses.name: Matthew 17:16
verses.text: I brought him to your disciples, but they could not cure him.”  <div eID="gen6990" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv242"/><div sID="gen6991" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv242"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Faithless and perverse generation!” </q>Jesus exclaimed, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“how long must I be among you? How long must I have patience with you? Bring the boy here to me.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 17:18
verses.text: Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy; and he was cured from that very hour.

verses.name: Matthew 17:19
verses.text: Afterwards the disciples came up to Jesus, and asked him privately: “Why was it that we could not drive it out?”  <div eID="gen6991" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv243"/><div sID="gen6992" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv243"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Because you have so little faith,” </q>he answered; <q marker="" who="Jesus">“for, I tell you, if your faith were only like a mustard seed, you could say to this mountain ‘Move from this place to that!’ and it would be moved; and nothing would be impossible to you.” </q>  <div eID="gen6992" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv244"/><div sID="gen6993" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv244"/> While Jesus and his disciples were together in Galilee, he said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The Son of Man is destined to be betrayed into human hands,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 17:23
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and they will put him to death, but on the third day he will rise.” </q>The disciples were greatly distressed.  <div eID="gen6993" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv245"/><div sID="gen6994" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv245"/> After they had reached Capernaum, the collectors of the Temple-rate came up to Peter, and said: “Does not your Master pay the Temple-rate?”  <div eID="gen6994" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 17:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv246"/><div sID="gen6995" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv246"/> “Yes,” answered Peter. But, on going into the house, before he could speak, Jesus said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“What do you think, Simon? From whom do earthly kings take taxes or tribute? From their sons, or from others?” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 17:26
verses.text: “From others,” answered Peter. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Well then,” </q>continued Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“their sons go free.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 17:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Still, so we don't offend them, go and throw a line into the Sea; take the first fish that rises, open its mouth, and you will find in it a piece of money. Take that, and give it to the collectors for both of us.” </q>  <div eID="gen6995" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv247"/><div sID="gen6996" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen6996" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.17"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:1
verses.text: On the same occasion the disciples came to Jesus, and asked him: “Who is really the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”

verses.name: Matthew 18:2
verses.text: Jesus called a little child to him, and placed it in the middle of them, and then said:

verses.name: Matthew 18:3
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you, unless you change and become like little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven at all.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore, anyone who will humble themselves like this child — that person will be the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And anyone who, for the sake of my name, welcomes even one little child like this, is welcoming me.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But, if anyone puts temptation in the way of one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be best for them to be sunk in the depths of the sea with a great millstone hung around their neck.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Alas for the world because of such temptations! There cannot but be temptations but sorrow awaits the person who does the tempting!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv247"/><div sID="gen6997" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv247"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off, and throw it away. It would be better for you to enter the life maimed or lame, than to have both hands, or both feet, and be thrown into the fire that never goes out.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">If your eye causes you to sin, take it out, and throw it away. It would be better for you to enter the life with only one eye, than to have both eyes and be thrown into the fires of Gehenna.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:10
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Beware of despising one of these little ones, for in heaven, I tell you, their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.</q>  <div eID="gen6997" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv248"/><div sID="gen6998" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv248"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">What think you? If a person owns a hundred sheep, and one of them strays, will the person not leave the ninety-nine on the hills, and go and search for the one that is straying?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:13
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And, if they succeed in finding it, I tell you that they rejoice more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine which did not stray.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:14
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So, too, it is the will of my Father who is in heaven that not one of these little ones should be lost.</q>  <div eID="gen6998" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv249"/><div sID="gen6999" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv249"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">If your brother or sister does wrong, go to them and convince them of their fault when you are both alone. If they listen to you, you have won them over.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:16
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But, if they do not listen to you, take with you one or two others, so that ‘on the evidence of two or three witnesses, every word may be put beyond dispute.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:17
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">If they refuse to listen to them, speak to the church; and, if they also refuse to listen to the church, treat him as you would a Gentile or a tax-gatherer.</q>  <div eID="gen6999" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv250"/><div sID="gen7000" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv250"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">I tell you, all that you forbid on earth will be held in heaven to be forbidden, and all that you allow on earth will be held in heaven to be allowed.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Again, I tell you that, if but two of you on earth agree as to what they will pray for, whatever it be, it will be granted them by my Father who is in heaven.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:20
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For where two or three have come together in my name, I am present with them.” </q>  <div eID="gen7000" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 18:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv251"/><div sID="gen7001" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv251"/> Then Peter came up, and said to Jesus: “Master, how often am I to forgive someone who wrongs me? As many as seven times?”

verses.name: Matthew 18:22
verses.text: But Jesus answered: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Not seven times, but ‘seventy times seven.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:23
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore the kingdom of heaven may be compared to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:24
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When he had begun to do so, one of them was brought to him who owed him ten thousand bags of gold;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and, as he could not pay, his master ordered him to be sold towards the payment of the debt, together with his wife, and his children, and everything that he had.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The servant threw himself down on the ground before him and said ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you all.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The master was moved with compassion; and he let him go, and forgave him the debt.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But, on going out, that same servant came upon one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred silver coins. Seizing him by the throat, he said ‘Pay what you owe me.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">His fellow servant threw himself on the ground and begged for mercy. ‘Have patience with me,’ he said, ‘and I will pay you.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But the other would not, but went and put him in prison until he should pay his debt.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:31
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and went to their master and laid the whole matter before him.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:32
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So the master sent for the servant, and said to him ‘You wicked servant! When you begged me for mercy, I forgave you the whole of that debt.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:33
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Ought not you, also, to have shown mercy to your fellow servant, just as I showed mercy to you?’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:34
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then his master, in anger, handed him over to the jailers, until he should pay the whole of his debt.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 18:35
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So, also, will my heavenly Father do to you, unless each one of you forgives his brother or sister from your heart.” </q>  <div eID="gen7001" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen6915" type="section"/> <chapter eID="Matt.18"/> <div eID="gen6853" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:1
verses.text: At the conclusion of this teaching, Jesus withdrew from Galilee, and went into that district of Judea which is on the other side of the Jordan.

verses.name: Matthew 19:2
verses.text: Great crowds followed him, and he cured them there.

verses.name: Matthew 19:3
verses.text: Presently some Pharisees came up to him, and, to test him, said: “Has a man the right to divorce his wife for every cause?”

verses.name: Matthew 19:4
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv252"/><div sID="gen7003" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv252"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Have not you read,” </q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“that at the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and said — ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother, and be united to his wife, and the man and his wife will become one’?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So that they are no longer two, but one. What God himself, then, has yoked together people must not separate.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:7
verses.text: “Why, then,” they said, “did Moses direct that a man should ‘serve his wife with a notice of separation and divorce her’?”  <div eID="gen7003" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv253"/><div sID="gen7004" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv253"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Moses, owing to the hardness of your hearts,” </q>answered Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“permitted you to divorce your wives, but that was not so at the beginning.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of some serious sexual sin, and marries another woman, is guilty of adultery.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:10
verses.text: “If that,” said the disciples, “is the position of a man with regard to his wife, it is better not to marry.”  <div eID="gen7004" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv254"/><div sID="gen7005" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv254"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“It is not everyone,” </q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“who can accept this teaching, but only those who have been enabled to do so.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Some men, it is true, have from birth been disabled for marriage, while others have been disabled by their fellow men, and others again have disabled themselves for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let him accept it who can.” </q>  <div eID="gen7005" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv255"/><div sID="gen7006" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv255"/> Then some little children were brought to Jesus, for him to place his hands on them, and pray; but the disciples found fault with those who had brought them.

verses.name: Matthew 19:14
verses.text: Jesus, however, said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for it is to the childlike that the kingdom of heaven belongs.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:15
verses.text: So he placed his hands on them, and then went on his way.  <div eID="gen7006" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv256"/><div sID="gen7007" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv256"/> A man came up to Jesus, and said: “Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?”  <div eID="gen7007" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv257"/><div sID="gen7008" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv257"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Why ask me about goodness?” </q>answered Jesus. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“There is but One who is good. If you want to enter the life, keep the commandments.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:18
verses.text: “What commandments?” asked the man. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“These,” </q>answered Jesus: — <q marker="" who="Jesus">“‘You must not kill. You must not commit adultery. You must not steal. You must not say what is false about others.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Honor your father and your mother.’ And ‘You must love your neighbor as you love yourself.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:20
verses.text: “I have observed all these,” said the young man. “What is still wanting in me?”  <div eID="gen7008" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv258"/><div sID="gen7009" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv258"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“If you wish to be perfect,” </q>answered Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“go and sell your property, and give to the poor, and you will have wealth in heaven; then come and follow me.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:22
verses.text: On hearing these words, the young man went away distressed, for he had great possessions.

verses.name: Matthew 19:23
verses.text: At this, Jesus said to his disciples: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you that a rich person will find it hard to enter the kingdom of heaven!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:24
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I say again, it is easier for a camel to get through a needle’s eye than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven!” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:25
verses.text: On hearing this, the disciples exclaimed in great astonishment: “Who then can possibly be saved?”

verses.name: Matthew 19:26
verses.text: But Jesus looked at them, and said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“With people this is impossible, but with God everything is possible.” </q>Then Peter turned and said to Jesus:

verses.name: Matthew 19:27
verses.text: “But we — we left everything, and followed you; what, then, will we have?”  <div eID="gen7009" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 19:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv259"/><div sID="gen7010" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv259"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you,” </q>answered Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“that at the new creation, ‘when the Son of Man takes his seat on his throne of glory,’ you who followed me will be seated on twelve thrones, as judges of the twelve tribes of Israel.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or land, for my sake, will receive many times as much, and will ‘gain eternal life.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 19:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But many who are first now will then be last, and those who are last will be first.</q>  <div eID="gen7010" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.19"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:1
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For the kingdom of heaven is like an employer who went out in the early morning to hire laborers for his vineyards.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:2
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">He agreed with the laborers to pay them the standard daily rate of two silver coins, and sent them into his vineyard.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:3
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">On going out again, about nine o’clock, he saw some others standing in the marketplace, doing nothing.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘You also may go into my vineyard,’ he said, ‘and I will pay you what is fair.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So they went. Going out again about midday and about three o’clock, he did as before.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When he went out about five, he found some others standing there, and said to them ‘Why have you been standing here all day long, doing nothing?’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered. ‘You also may go into my vineyard,’ he said.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">In the evening the owner of the vineyard said to his steward ‘Call the laborers, and pay them their wages, beginning with the last, and ending with the first.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Now when those who had been hired about five o’clock went up, they received two silver coins each.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:10
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So, when the first went up, they thought that they would receive more, but they also received two silver coins each;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">on which they began to grumble at their employer.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘These last,’ they said, ‘have done only one hour’s work, and yet you have put them on the same footing with us, who have borne the brunt of the day’s work, and the heat.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:13
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘My friend,’ was his reply to one of them, ‘I am not treating you unfairly. Did not you agree with me for two silver coins?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:14
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Take what belongs to you, and go. I choose to give to this last man the same as to you.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:15
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Have not I the right to do as I choose with what is mine? Are you envious because I am liberal?’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:16
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So those who are last will be first, and the first last.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv260"/><div sID="gen7011" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv260"/> When Jesus was on the point of going up to Jerusalem, he gathered the twelve disciples around him by themselves, and said to them as they were on their way:

verses.name: Matthew 20:18
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem; and there the Son of Man will be betrayed to the chief priests and teachers of the law, and they will condemn him to death,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and give him up to the Gentiles for them to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify; and on the third day he will rise.” </q>  <div eID="gen7011" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv261"/><div sID="gen7012" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv261"/> Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to him with her sons, bowing to the ground, and begging a favor.

verses.name: Matthew 20:21
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“What is it that you want?” </q>he asked. “I want you to say,” she replied, “that in your kingdom these two sons of mine may sit, one on your right, and the other on your left.”  <div eID="gen7012" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv262"/><div sID="gen7013" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv262"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“You do not know what you are asking,” </q>was Jesus’ answer. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Can you drink the cup that I am to drink?” </q>“Yes,” they exclaimed, “we can.”  <div eID="gen7013" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv263"/><div sID="gen7014" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv263"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“You will indeed drink my cup,” </q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“but as to a seat at my right and at my left — that is not mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:24
verses.text: On hearing of this, the ten others were very indignant about the two brothers.

verses.name: Matthew 20:25
verses.text: Jesus, however, called the ten to him, and said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them as you know, and their high officials oppress them.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Among you it is not so.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">No, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to take the first place among you, must be your slave;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 20:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">just as the Son of Man came, not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.” </q>  <div eID="gen7014" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 20:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv264"/><div sID="gen7015" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv264"/> As they were going out of Jericho, a great crowd followed him.

verses.name: Matthew 20:30
verses.text: Two blind men who were sitting by the roadside, hearing that Jesus was passing, called out: “Take pity on us, Master, Son of David!”

verses.name: Matthew 20:31
verses.text: The crowd told them to be quiet; but the men only called out the louder: “Take pity on us, Master, Son of David!”

verses.name: Matthew 20:32
verses.text: Then Jesus stopped and called them. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“What do you want me to do for you?” </q>he said.

verses.name: Matthew 20:33
verses.text: “Master,” they replied, “we want our eyes to be opened.”

verses.name: Matthew 20:34
verses.text: So Jesus, moved with compassion, touched their eyes, and immediately they recovered their sight, and followed him.  <div eID="gen7015" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.20"/> <div eID="gen7002" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:1
verses.text: When they had almost reached Jerusalem, having come as far as Bethphage, on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent on two disciples.

verses.name: Matthew 21:2
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Go to the village facing you,” </q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“and you will immediately find an ass tethered, with a foal by her side; untie her, and lead her here for me.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:3
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And, if anyone says anything to you, you are to say this — ‘The Master wants them’; and he will send them at once.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:4
verses.text: This happened in fulfillment of these words in the prophet —

verses.name: Matthew 21:5
verses.text: ‘Say to the people of Zion — “Your King is coming to you, gentle, and riding on an ass, and on the foal of a beast of burden.”’

verses.name: Matthew 21:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv265"/><div sID="gen7017" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv265"/> So the disciples went and did as Jesus had directed them.

verses.name: Matthew 21:7
verses.text: They led the ass and the foal back, and, when they had put their cloaks on them, he seated himself on them.

verses.name: Matthew 21:8
verses.text: The immense crowd of people spread their cloaks in the road, while some cut branches off the trees, and spread them on the road.

verses.name: Matthew 21:9
verses.text: The crowds that led the way, as well as those that followed behind, kept shouting: “God save the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! God save him from on high!”

verses.name: Matthew 21:10
verses.text: When he had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred, and asked —

verses.name: Matthew 21:11
verses.text: “Who is this?”, to which the crowd replied — “This is the prophet Jesus from Nazareth in Galilee.”  <div eID="gen7017" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv266"/><div sID="gen7018" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv266"/> Jesus went into the Temple Courts, and drove out all those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers, and the seats of the pigeon-dealers,

verses.name: Matthew 21:13
verses.text: and said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Scripture says ‘My house will be called a house of prayer’; but you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:14
verses.text: While he was still in the Temple Courts, some blind and some lame people came up to him, and he cured them.

verses.name: Matthew 21:15
verses.text: But, when the chief priests and the teachers of the law saw the wonderful things that Jesus did, and the boys who were calling out in the Temple Courts “God save the Son of David!”, they were indignant,

verses.name: Matthew 21:16
verses.text: and said to him: “Do you hear what these boys are saying?” <div eID="gen7018" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7019" type="paragraph"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Yes,” </q>answered Jesus; <q marker="" who="Jesus">“but did you never read the words — ‘Out of the mouths of babes and sucklings you have called forth perfect praise’?” </q>  <div eID="gen7019" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv267"/><div sID="gen7020" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv267"/> Then he left them, and went out of the city to Bethany, and spent the night there.  <div eID="gen7020" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv268"/><div sID="gen7021" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv268"/> The next morning, in returning to the city, Jesus became hungry;

verses.name: Matthew 21:19
verses.text: and, noticing a solitary fig tree by the roadside, he went up to it, but found nothing on it but leaves. So he said to it: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Never again will fruit be gathered off you.” </q>And suddenly the fruit tree withered up.

verses.name: Matthew 21:20
verses.text: When the disciples saw this, they exclaimed in astonishment: “How suddenly the fig tree withered up!”  <div eID="gen7021" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv269"/><div sID="gen7022" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv269"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you,” </q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“if you have faith, without ever a doubt, you will do what not only what has been done to the fig tree, but, even if you should say to this hill ‘Be lifted up and hurled into the sea!’ it would be done.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:22
