verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And whatever you ask for in your prayers will, if you have faith, be granted you.” </q>  <div eID="gen7022" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv270"/><div sID="gen7023" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv270"/> After Jesus had come into the Temple Courts, the chief priests and the councillors of the Nation came up to him as he was teaching, and said: “What authority have you to do these things? Who gave you this authority?”  <div eID="gen7023" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv271"/><div sID="gen7024" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv271"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I, too,” </q>said Jesus in reply, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“will ask you one question; if you will give me an answer to it, then I, also, will tell you what authority I have to act as I do.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">It is about John’s baptism. What was its origin? Divine or human?” But they began arguing among themselves: “If we say ‘divine,’ he will say to us ‘Why then did not you believe him?’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:26
verses.text: But if we say ‘human,’ we are afraid of the people, for everyone regards John as a prophet.”

verses.name: Matthew 21:27
verses.text: So the answer they gave Jesus was — “We do not know.” <div eID="gen7024" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7025" type="paragraph"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Then I,” </q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“refuse to tell you what authority I have to do these things.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">What do you think of this? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the elder and said ‘Go and work in the vineyard today my son.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘Yes, sir,’ he answered; but he did not go.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then the father went to the second son, and said the same. ‘I will not,’ he answered; but afterwards he was sorry and went.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:31
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Which of the two sons did as his father wished?” </q>“The second,” they said. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you,” </q>added Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“that tax-gatherers and prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God before you.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:32
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For when John came to you, walking in the path of righteousness, you did not believe him, but tax-gatherers and prostitutes did; and yet you, though you saw this, even then were not sorry, nor did you believe him.</q>  <div eID="gen7025" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv272"/><div sID="gen7026" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv272"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">Listen to another parable. A man, who was an employer, once planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, built a tower, and then let it out to tenants and went abroad.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:34
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When the time for the grape harvest drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants, to receive his share of the produce.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:35
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But the tenants seized his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:36
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">A second time the owner sent some servants, a larger number than before, and the tenants treated them in the same way.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:37
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">As a last resource he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:38
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But the tenants, on seeing his son, said to each other ‘Here is the heir! Come, let us kill him, and get his inheritance.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:39
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So they seized him, and threw him outside the vineyard, and killed him.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:40
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Now, when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:41
verses.text: “Miserable wretches!” they exclaimed, “he will put them to a miserable death, and he will let out the vineyard to other tenants, who will pay him his share of the produce at the proper times.”

verses.name: Matthew 21:42
verses.text: Then Jesus added: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Have you never read in the scriptures? — ‘The stone which the builders despised — Has now itself become the corner-stone; This corner-stone has come from the Lord, and is marvelous in our eyes.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:43
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">That, I tell you, is why the kingdom of God will be taken from you, and given to a nation that does produce the fruit of the kingdom.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 21:44
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Yes, and he who falls on this stone will be dashed to pieces, while anyone on whom it falls — it will scatter him as dust.” </q>  <div eID="gen7026" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 21:45
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv273"/><div sID="gen7027" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv273"/> After listening to these parables, the chief priests and the Pharisees saw that it was about them that he was speaking;

verses.name: Matthew 21:46
verses.text: yet, although eager to arrest him, they were afraid of the crowds, who regarded him as a prophet.  <div eID="gen7027" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv274"/><div sID="gen7028" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7028" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.21"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:1
verses.text: Once more Jesus spoke to them in parables.

verses.name: Matthew 22:2
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The kingdom of heaven,” he said, “may be compared to a king who gave a banquet in honor of his son’s wedding.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:3
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">He sent his servants to call those who had been invited to the banquet, but they were unwilling to come.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">A second time he sent some servants, with orders to say to those who had been invited ‘I have prepared my breakfast, my cattle and fat beasts are killed and everything is ready; come to the banquet.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">They, however, took no notice, but went off, one to their farm, another to their business;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">while the rest, seizing his servants, ill-treated them and killed them.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The king, in anger, sent his troops, put those murderers to death, and set their city on fire.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then he said to his servants ‘The banquet is prepared, but those who were invited were not worthy.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So go to the cross-roads, and invite everyone you find to the banquet.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:10
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The servants went out into the roads and collected all the people whom they found, whether bad or good; and the bridal-hall was filled with guests.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But, when the king went in to see his guests, he noticed there a man who had not put on a wedding-robe.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So he said to him ‘My friend, how is it that you came in here without a wedding-robe?’ The man was speechless.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:13
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then the king said to the attendants ‘Tie him hand and foot, and ‘put him out into the darkness’ outside, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:14
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For many are called, but few chosen.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv274"/><div sID="gen7029" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv274"/> Then the Pharisees went away and conferred together as to how they might lay a trap for Jesus in the course of conversation.

verses.name: Matthew 22:16
verses.text: They sent their disciples, with the Herodians, to say to him: “Teacher, we know that you are an honest person, and that you teach the way of God honestly, and are not afraid of anyone; for you pay no regard to a person’s position.

verses.name: Matthew 22:17
verses.text: Tell us, then, what you think. Are we right in paying taxes to the Emperor, or not?”

verses.name: Matthew 22:18
verses.text: Perceiving their malice, Jesus answered: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Why are you testing me, you hypocrites?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Show me the coin with which the tax is paid.” </q>And, when they had brought him a coin,

verses.name: Matthew 22:20
verses.text: he asked: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Whose head and title are these?” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:21
verses.text: “The Emperor’s,” they answered: on which he said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Then pay to the Emperor what belongs to the Emperor, and to God what belongs to God.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:22
verses.text: They wondered at his answer, and left him alone and went away.  <div eID="gen7029" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv275"/><div sID="gen7030" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv275"/> That same day some Sadducees came up to Jesus, maintaining that there is no resurrection. Their question was this: —

verses.name: Matthew 22:24
verses.text: “Teacher, Moses said — ‘should a man die without children, the man’s brother will become the husband of the widow, and raise a family for his brother.’

verses.name: Matthew 22:25
verses.text: Now we had living among us seven brothers; of whom the eldest married and died, and, as he had no family, left his wife for his brother.

verses.name: Matthew 22:26
verses.text: The same thing happened to the second and the third brothers, and indeed to all the seven.

verses.name: Matthew 22:27
verses.text: The woman herself died last of all.

verses.name: Matthew 22:28
verses.text: At the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be out of the seven, all of them having been married to her?”  <div eID="gen7030" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv276"/><div sID="gen7031" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv276"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Your mistake,” </q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“is due to your ignorance of the scriptures, and of the power of God.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For at the resurrection there is no marrying or being married, but all who rise are as angels in heaven.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:31
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">As to the resurrection of the dead, have you not read these words of God — </q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:32
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of dead people, but of living.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:33
verses.text: The crowds, who had been listening to him, were greatly struck with his teaching.  <div eID="gen7031" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 22:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv277"/><div sID="gen7032" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv277"/> When the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they collected together.

verses.name: Matthew 22:35
verses.text: Then one of them, a Student of the law, to test him, asked this question —

verses.name: Matthew 22:36
verses.text: “Teacher, what is the great commandment in the law?”

verses.name: Matthew 22:37
verses.text: His answer was: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“‘You must love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:38
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">This is the great first commandment.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:39
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The second, which is like it, is this — ‘You must love your neighbor as you love yourself.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:40
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:41
verses.text: Before the Pharisees separated, Jesus put this question to them —

verses.name: Matthew 22:42
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” </q>“David’s,” they said.

verses.name: Matthew 22:43
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“How is it, then,” </q>Jesus replied, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“that David, speaking under inspiration, calls him ‘lord,’ in the passage — </q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:44
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘The Lord said to my Lord: “Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies beneath your feet”’?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:45
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Since, then, David calls him ‘lord,’ how is he David’s son?” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 22:46
verses.text: No one could say a word in answer; nor did anyone after that day venture to question him further.  <div eID="gen7032" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv278"/><div sID="gen7033" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7033" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.22"/>

verses.name: Matthew 23:1
verses.text: Then Jesus speaking to the crowds and to his disciples, said:

verses.name: Matthew 23:2
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The teachers of the law and the Pharisees now occupy the chair of Moses.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:3
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore practice and lay to heart everything that they tell preach but do not practice.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">While they make up heavy loads and pile them on other people’s shoulder’s they decline, themselves, to lift a finger to move them.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">All their actions are done to attract attention. They widen their phylacteries, and increase the size of their tassels,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and like to have the place of honor at dinner, and the best seats in the Synagogues,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and to be greeted in the markets with respect, and to be called ‘Rabbi’ for everybody.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But do not allow yourselves to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have only one teacher, and you yourselves are all brothers and sisters.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And do not call anyone on the earth your ‘Father,’ for your have only one Father, the heavenly Father.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:10
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Nor must you allow yourselves to be called ‘leaders,’ for you have only one leader, the Christ.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The person who wants to be the greatest among you must be your servant.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Whoever exalts themselves will be humbled, and whoever humbles themselves will be exalted.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:13
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But alas for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, hypocrites that you are! You turn the key of the kingdom of heaven in people’s faces. For you do not go in yourselves, and do not allow those who try to go in to do so.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:14
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Alas for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, hypocrites that you are! You destroy widow’s houses, even while pretending to make long prayers; therefore you will receive greater condemnation.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:15
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Alas for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, hypocrites that you are! You scour land and sea to make a single convert, and, when they are gained, you make them twice as deserving of Gehenna as you are yourselves.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:16
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Alas for you, you blind guides! You say ‘if any answer by the Temple, their oath counts for nothing; but, if anyone swears by the gold of the Temple, their oath is binding them’!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:17
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Fools that you are and blind! Which is the more important? The gold? Or the Temple which has given sacredness to the gold?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:18
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">You say, too, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, their oath counts for nothing, but, if anyone swears by the offering placed on it, their oath is binding on them’!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Blind indeed! Which is the more important? The offering? Or the altar which gives sacredness to the offering?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:20
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore a person, swearing by the altar, swears by it and by all that is on it,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:21
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and a person, swearing by the Temple, swears by it and by him who dwells in it,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:22
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">while a person, swearing by heaven, swears by the throne of God, and by him who sits on it.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:23
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Alas for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, hypocrites that you are! You pay tithes on mint, fennel, and caraway seed, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law — justice, mercy, and good faith. These last you ought to have put into practice, without neglecting the first.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:24
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">You blind guides, to strain out a gnat and to swallow a camel!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Alas for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, hypocrites that you are! You clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are filled with the results of greed and self-indulgence.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">You blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the dish, so that the outside may become clean as well.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Alas for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, hypocrites that you are! You are like whitewashed tombs, which indeed look fair outside, while inside they are filled with dead people’s bones and all kinds of filth.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">It is the same with you. Outwardly, and to others, you have the look of religious people, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and sin.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Alas for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, hypocrites that you are! You build the tombs of the prophets, and decorate the monuments of religious people,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and say ‘Had we been living in the days of our ancestors, we should have taken part in their murder of the prophets!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:31
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">By doing this you are furnishing evidence against yourselves that you are true children of the people who murdered the prophets.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:32
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Fill up the measure of your ancestor’s guilt.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:33
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">You snakes and children of snakes! How can you escape being sentenced to Gehenna?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:34
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">That is why I send you prophets, wise people, and teachers of the law, some of whom you will crucify and kill, and some of whom you will scourge in your Synagogues, and persecute from town to town;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:35
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">in order the blood on your heads may fall every drop of innocent ‘blood split on earth,’ from the blood of innocent Abel down to that of Zechariah, Barachiah’s son, whom you murdered between the Temple and the altar.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:36
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">All this, I tell you, will come home to the present generation.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:37
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Jerusalem! Jerusalem! She who slays the prophets and stones the messengers sent to her — Oh, how often have I wished to gather your children around me, as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you would not come!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:38
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Verily, your house is left to you desolate!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 23:39
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For nevermore, I tell you, will you see me, until you say — ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!’” </q>  <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv278"/><div sID="gen7034" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7034" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.23"/>

verses.name: Matthew 24:1
verses.text: Leaving the Temple Courts, Jesus was walking away, when his disciples came up to draw his attention to the Temple buildings.

verses.name: Matthew 24:2
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Do you see all these things?” </q>was his answer. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you, not a single stone will be left here on another, which will not be thrown down,” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:3
verses.text: so, while Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came up to him privately and said: “Tell us when this will be, and what will be the sign of your coming, and of the close of the age.”

verses.name: Matthew 24:4
verses.text: Jesus replied to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“See that no one leads you astray;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for, many will take my name, and come saying ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">You will hear of wars and rumors of wars; take care not to be alarmed, for such things must occur; but the end is not yet here.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For ‘nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom,’ and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">All this, however, will be but the beginning of the birth pangs!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When that time comes, they will give you up to persecution, and will put you to death, and you will be hated by all nations because of me.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:10
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And then many will fall away, and will betray one another, and hate one another.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Many false prophets, also, will appear and lead many astray;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and, owing to the increase of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:13
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Yet the person who endures to the end will be saved.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:14
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">This good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the world as a witness to all nations; and then will come the end.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:15
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">As soon, then, as you see ‘the Foul Desecration,’ mentioned by the prophet Daniel, standing in the Holy place,” </q>(the reader must consider what this means)

verses.name: Matthew 24:16
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“then those of you who are in Judea must take refuge in the mountains;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:17
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and a man on the housetop must not go down to get the things that are in his house;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:18
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">nor must one who is on their farm turn back to get his cloak.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Alas for pregnant women, and for those who are nursing infants in those days!</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:20
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Pray, too, that your flight may not take place in winter, nor on a Sabbath;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:21
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for that will be ‘a time of great distress, the like of which has not occurred from the beginning of the world down to the present time’ — no, nor ever will again.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:22
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Had not those days been limited, not a single soul would escape; but for the sake of ‘God’s people’ a limit will be put to them.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:23
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">At that time, if anyone should say to you ‘Look! Here is the Christ!’ or ‘Here he is!’, do not believe it;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:24
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for false Christs and false prophets will arise, and will display great signs and marvels, so that, were it possible, even God’s people would be led astray.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Remember, I have told you beforehand.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore, if people say to you ‘He is in the wilderness!’, do not go out there; or ‘He is in an inner room!’, do not believe it;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for, just as lightning will start from the east and flash across to the west, so will it be with the coming of the Son of Man.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Wherever a dead body lies, there will the vultures flock.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Immediately after the distress of those days, ‘the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give her light, the stars will fall from the heavens,’ and ‘the forces of the heavens will be convulsed.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then will appear the sign of the Son of Man in the heavens; and all the peoples of the earth will mourn, when they see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the heavens,’ with power and great glory;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:31
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and he will send his angels, with a great trumpet, and they will gather his people around him from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv278"/><div sID="gen7035" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv278"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">Learn the lesson taught by the fig tree. As soon as its branches are full of sap, and it is bursting into leaf, you know that summer is near.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:33
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And so may you, as soon as you see all these things, know that he is at your doors.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:34
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I tell you, even the present generation will not pass away, until all these things have taken place.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:35
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The heavens and the earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:36
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But about that day and hour, no one knows — not even the angels of heaven, not even the Son — but only the Father himself.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:37
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For, just as in the days of Noah, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:38
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">In those days before the flood they went on eating and drinking, marrying and being married, up to the very day on which Noah entered the ark,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:39
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">taking not notice until the flood came and swept them one and all away; and so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:40
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">At that time, of two men on a farm one will be taken and one left;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:41
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">of two women grinding with the hand-mill one will be taken and one left.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:42
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore watch; for you cannot be sure on what day your Master is coming.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:43
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But this you do know, that, had the owner of the house known at what time of night the thief was coming, they would have been on the watch, and would not have allowed their house to be broken into.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:44
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore, you must also prepare, since it is just when you are least expecting him that the Son of Man will come.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:45
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Who, then is that trustworthy, careful servant, who has been placed by their master over his household, to give them their food at the proper time?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:46
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Happy will that servant be whom their master, when he comes home, will find doing this.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:47
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I tell you that their master will put them in charge of the whole of his property.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:48
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But, should the servant be a bad servant, and say to themselves ‘My master is a long time in coming,’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:49
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and begin to beat their fellow servants, and eat and drink with drunkards,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:50
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">that servant’s master will come on a day when they do not expect him, and at an hour of which they are unaware,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 24:51
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and will flog the servant severely, and assign them their place among the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.</q>  <div eID="gen7035" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv279"/><div sID="gen7036" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7036" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.24"/>

verses.name: Matthew 25:1
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went out to meet the groom.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:2
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Five of them were foolish, and five were prudent.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:3
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The foolish ones took their lamps, but took no oil with them;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">while the prudent ones, besides taking their lamps, took oil in their jars.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">As the groom was late in coming, they all became drowsy, and slept.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But at midnight a shout was raised — ‘The groom is coming! Come out to meet him!’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then all the bridesmaids woke up and trimmed their lamps,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and the foolish said to the prudent ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But the prudent ones answered ‘No, There may not be enough for you and for us. Go instead to those who sell it, and buy for yourselves.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:10
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But while they were on their way to buy it, the groom came; and the bridesmaids who were ready went in with him to the banquet, and the door was shut.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Afterwards the other bridesmaids came. ‘Sir, Sir,’ they said, ‘open the door to us!’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But the groom answered ‘I tell you, I do not know you.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:13
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore watch, since you know neither the day nor the hour.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv279"/><div sID="gen7037" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv279"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">For it is as though a man, going on his travels, called his servants, and gave his property into their charge.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:15
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">He gave five bags of gold to one, two to another, and one bag to a third, in proportion to the ability of each. Then he set out on his travels.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:16
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The servant who had received the five bags of gold went at once and traded with it, and made another five bags.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:17
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So, too, the servant who had received the two bags of gold made another two bags.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:18
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But the servant who had received the one bag went and dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">After a long time the master of those servants returned, and settled accounts with them.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:20
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The servant who had received the five bags of gold came up and brought five bags more. ‘Sir,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with five bags of gold; look, I have made another five bags!’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:21
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘Well done, good, trustworthy servant!’ said his master. ‘You have been trustworthy with a small sum; now I will place a large one in your hands; come and share your master’s joy!’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:22
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then the one who had received the two bags of gold came up and said ‘Sir, you entrusted me with two bags pounds; look, I have made another two!’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:23
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘Well done, good, trustworthy servant!’ said his master. ‘You have been trustworthy with a small sum; now I will place a large one in your hands; come and share your master’s joy!’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:24
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The man who had received the single bag of gold came up, too, and said ‘Sir, I knew that you were a hard man; you reap where you have not sown, and gather up where you have not winnowed;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and, in my fear, I went and hid your money in the ground; look, here is what belongs to you!’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘You lazy, worthless servant!’ was his master’s reply. ‘You knew that I reap where I have not sown, and gather up where I have not winnowed?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then you ought to have placed my money in the hands of bankers, and I, on my return, should have received my money, with interest.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘Therefore,’ he continued, ‘take away from him the one bag of gold, and give it to the one who has the ten bags.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For, to him who has, more will be given, and he will have abundance; but, as for him who has nothing, even what he has will be taken away from him.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">As for the useless servant, ‘put him out into the darkness’ outside, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.’</q>  <div eID="gen7037" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 25:31
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv280"/><div sID="gen7038" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv280"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">When the Son of Man has come in his glory and all the angels with him, then he ‘will take his seat on his throne of glory’;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:32
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate the people — just as a shepherd separates sheep from goats — </q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:33
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">placing the sheep on his right hand, and the goats on his left.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:34
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then the king will say to those on his right ‘Come, you who are blessed by my Father, enter into possession of the kingdom prepared for you ever since the beginning of the world.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:35
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For, when I was hungry, you gave me food; when I was thirsty, you gave me drink; when I was a stranger, you took me to your homes;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:36
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">when I was naked, you clothed me; when I fell ill, you visited me; and when I was in prison, you came to me.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:37
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then the righteous will answer ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, and feed you? Or thirsty, and give you a drink?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:38
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When did we see you a stranger, and take you to our homes? Or naked, and clothe you?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:39
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When did we see you ill, or in prison, and come to you?’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:40
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And the king will reply ‘I tell you, as often as you did it to one of these my brothers or sisters, however unimportant they seemed, you did it to me.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:41
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then he will say to those on his left ‘Go from my presence, accursed, into the ‘permanent fire which has been prepared for the devil and his angels.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:42
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For, when I was hungry, you gave me no food; when I was thirsty, you gave me no drink;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:43
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">when I was a stranger, you did not take me to your homes; when I was naked, you did not clothe me; and, when I was ill and in prison, you did not visit me.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:44
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then they, in their turn, will answer ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or ill, or in prison, and did not supply your wants?’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:45
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And then he will reply ‘I tell you, as often as you failed to do it to one of these, however unimportant, you failed to do it to me.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 25:46
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And these last will go away ‘into lasting correction,’ but the righteous ‘into lasting life.’” </q>  <div eID="gen7038" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv281"/><div sID="gen7039" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7039" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.25"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:1
verses.text: When Jesus had finished teaching all of that, he said to his disciples:

verses.name: Matthew 26:2
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“You know that in two days time the Festival of the Passover will be here; and that the Son of Man is to be given up to be crucified.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:3
verses.text: Then the chief priests and the councillors of the Nation met in the house of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,

verses.name: Matthew 26:4
verses.text: and plotted together to arrest Jesus by stealth and put him to death;

verses.name: Matthew 26:5
verses.text: but they said: “Not during the Festival, or the people may riot.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv281"/><div sID="gen7040" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv281"/> After Jesus had reached Bethany, and while he was in the house of Simon the leper,

verses.name: Matthew 26:7
verses.text: a woman came up to him with an alabaster jar of very costly perfume, and poured the perfume on his head as he sat at the table.

verses.name: Matthew 26:8
verses.text: The disciples were indignant at seeing this. “What is this waste for?” they exclaimed.

verses.name: Matthew 26:9
verses.text: “It could have been sold for a large sum, and the money given to poor people.”  <div eID="gen7040" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv282"/><div sID="gen7041" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv282"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Why are you troubling the woman?” </q>Jesus said, when he noticed it. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“For this is a beautiful deed that she has done to me.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">You always have the poor with you, but you will not always have me.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">In pouring this perfume on my body, she has done it for my burying.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:13
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I tell you, wherever, in the whole world, this good news is proclaimed, what this woman has done will be told in memory of her.” </q>  <div eID="gen7041" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv283"/><div sID="gen7042" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv283"/> It was then that one of the Twelve, named Judas Iscariot, made his way to the chief priests,

verses.name: Matthew 26:15
verses.text: and said “What are you willing to give me, if I betray Jesus to you?” The Priests ‘weighed him out thirty pieces of silver’ as payment.

verses.name: Matthew 26:16
verses.text: So from that time Judas looked for an opportunity to betray Jesus.  <div eID="gen7042" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv284"/><div sID="gen7043" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv284"/> On the first day of the Festival of the unleavened bread, the disciples came up to Jesus, and said: “Where do you wish us to make preparations for you to eat the Passover?”  <div eID="gen7043" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv285"/><div sID="gen7044" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv285"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Go into the city to a certain man,” </q>he answered, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“and say to him ‘The teacher says — My time is near. I will keep the Passover with my disciples at your house.’” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:19
verses.text: The disciples did as Jesus directed them, and prepared the Passover.

verses.name: Matthew 26:20
verses.text: In the evening Jesus took his place with the twelve disciples,

verses.name: Matthew 26:21
verses.text: and, while they were eating, he said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you that one of you will betray me.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:22
verses.text: In great grief they began to say to him, one by one: “Can it be I, Master?”  <div eID="gen7044" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:23
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv286"/><div sID="gen7045" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv286"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The one who dipped his bread beside me in the dish,” </q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“is the one who will betray me.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:24
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">True, the Son of Man must go, as scripture says of him, yet alas for that man by whom the Son of Man is being betrayed! For that man ‘it would be better never to have been born!’” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:25
verses.text: Judas, who was betraying him, turned to him and said: “Can it be I, Rabbi?” <div eID="gen7045" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7046" type="paragraph"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“It is,” </q>answered Jesus.  <div eID="gen7046" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv287"/><div sID="gen7047" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv287"/> While they were eating, Jesus took some bread, and, after saying the blessing, broke it and, as he gave it to his disciples, said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Take it and eat it; this is my body.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:27
verses.text: Then he took a cup, and, after saying the thanksgiving, gave it to them, with the words: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Drink from it, all of you;</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for this is my covenant blood, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I tell you that I will never, after this, drink of this juice of the grape, until that day when I will drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.” </q>  <div eID="gen7047" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv288"/><div sID="gen7048" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv288"/> They then sang a hymn, and went out to the Mount of Olives.

verses.name: Matthew 26:31
verses.text: Then Jesus said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Even you will all fall away from me tonight. Scripture says — ‘I will strike down the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:32
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But, after I have risen, I will go before you into Galilee.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:33
verses.text: “If everyone else falls away from you,” Peter answered, “I will never fall away!”  <div eID="gen7048" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv289"/><div sID="gen7049" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv289"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you,” </q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“that this very night, before the cock crows, you will disown me three times!” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:35
verses.text: “Even if I must die with you,” Peter exclaimed, “I will never disown you!” All the disciples spoke in the same way.  <div eID="gen7049" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:36
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv290"/><div sID="gen7050" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv290"/> Then Jesus came with them to a garden called Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Sit down here while I go and pray over there.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:37
verses.text: Taking with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to show signs of sadness and deep distress of mind.

verses.name: Matthew 26:38
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I am sad at heart,” </q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“sad even to death; wait here and watch with me.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:39
verses.text: Going on a little further, he threw himself on his face in prayer. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“My Father,” </q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“if it is possible, let me be spared this cup; only, not as I will, but as you will.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:40
verses.text: Then he came to his disciples, and found them asleep. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“What!” </q>he said to Peter, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“could none of you watch with me for one hour?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:41
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Watch and pray so that you don't fall into temptation. True, the spirit is eager, but human nature is weak.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:42
verses.text: Again, a second time, he went away, and prayed. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“My Father,” </q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“if I cannot be spared this cup, but must drink it, your will be done!” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:43
verses.text: And coming back again he found them asleep, for their eyes were heavy.

verses.name: Matthew 26:44
verses.text: So he left them, and went away again, and prayed a third time, again saying the same words.

verses.name: Matthew 26:45
verses.text: Then he came to the disciples, and said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Sleep on now, and rest yourselves. Look - my time is close at hand, and the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of wicked people.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:46
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Up, and let us be going. Look! My betrayer is close at hand.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:47
verses.text: And, while he was still speaking, Judas, who was one of the Twelve, came in sight; and with him was a great crowd of people, with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and councillors of the nation.

verses.name: Matthew 26:48
verses.text: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them. “The man whom I kiss,” he had said, “will be the one; arrest him.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:49
verses.text: So he went up to Jesus at once, and exclaimed: “Welcome, Rabbi!” and kissed him;

verses.name: Matthew 26:50
verses.text: on which Jesus said to him: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Friend, do what you have come for.” </q>The men went up, seized Jesus, and arrested him.

verses.name: Matthew 26:51
verses.text: Suddenly one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and striking the high priest’s servant, cut off his ear.

verses.name: Matthew 26:52
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Sheathe your sword,” </q>Jesus said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“for all who draw the sword will be put to the sword.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:53
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Do you think that I cannot ask my Father for help, when he would at once send to my aid more than twelve legions of angels?</q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:54
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But in that case how would the scriptures be fulfilled, which say that this must be?” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:55
verses.text: Jesus at the same time said to the crowds: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Have you come out, as if after a robber, with swords and clubs, to take me? I have sat teaching day after day in the Temple Courts, and yet you did not arrest me.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:56
verses.text: The whole of this occurred in fulfillment of the Prophetic scriptures. Then the disciples all forsook him and fled.  <div eID="gen7050" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:57
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv291"/><div sID="gen7051" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv291"/> Those who had arrested Jesus took him to Caiaphas, the high priest, where the teachers of the law and the councillors had assembled.

verses.name: Matthew 26:58
verses.text: Peter followed him at a distance as far as the courtyard of the offices, to see the end.

verses.name: Matthew 26:59
verses.text: Meanwhile the chief priests and the whole of the High Council were trying to get such false evidence against Jesus, as would warrant putting him to death,

verses.name: Matthew 26:60
verses.text: but they did not find any, although many came forward with false evidence. Later on, however, two men came forward and said:

verses.name: Matthew 26:61
verses.text: “This man said ‘I am able to destroy the Temple of God, and to build it in three days.’”

verses.name: Matthew 26:62
verses.text: Then the high priest stood up, and said to Jesus: “Have you no answer? What is this evidence which these men are giving against you?”

verses.name: Matthew 26:63
verses.text: But Jesus remained silent. The high priest said to him: “I order you, by the living God, to tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”  <div eID="gen7051" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 26:64
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv292"/><div sID="gen7052" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv292"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“It is true,” </q>Jesus answered; <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Moreover I tell you all that hereafter you will ‘see the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of the Almighty, and coming on the clouds of the heavens.’” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 26:65
verses.text: Then the high priest tore his robes. “This is blasphemy!” he exclaimed. “Why do we want any more witnesses? You have just heard his blasphemy!

verses.name: Matthew 26:66
verses.text: What is your decision?” They answered: “He deserves death.”

verses.name: Matthew 26:67
verses.text: Then they spat in his face, and struck him, while others dealt blows at him, saying as they did so:

verses.name: Matthew 26:68
verses.text: “Now play the prophet for us, you Christ! Who was it that struck you?”

verses.name: Matthew 26:69
verses.text: Peter, meanwhile, was sitting outside in the courtyard; and a maidservant came up to him, and exclaimed: “Why, you were with Jesus the Galilean!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:70
verses.text: But Peter denied it before them all. “I do not know what you mean,” he replied.

verses.name: Matthew 26:71
verses.text: When he had gone out into the gateway, another maid saw him, and said to those who were there: “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:72
verses.text: Again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the man!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:73
verses.text: But soon afterwards those who were standing by came up and said to Peter: “You also are certainly one of them; why, even your way of speaking proves it!”

verses.name: Matthew 26:74
verses.text: Then Peter said: “I swear that I do not know the man! May God punish me if I am lying!” At that moment a cock crowed;

verses.name: Matthew 26:75
verses.text: and Peter remembered the words which Jesus had said — <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘Before a cock has crowed, you will disown me three times’;</q>and he went outside, and wept bitterly.  <div eID="gen7052" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv293"/><div sID="gen7053" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7053" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.26"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:1
verses.text: At daybreak all the chief priests and the councillors of the nation consulted together against Jesus, to bring about his death.

verses.name: Matthew 27:2
verses.text: They put him in chains and led him away, and gave him up to the Roman Governor, Pilate.

verses.name: Matthew 27:3
verses.text: Then Judas, who betrayed him, seeing that Jesus was condemned, repented of what he had done, and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and councillors.

verses.name: Matthew 27:4
verses.text: “I did wrong in betraying a good man to his death,” he said. “What has that to do with us?” they replied. “You must see to that yourself.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:5
verses.text: Judas flung down the pieces of silver in the Temple, and left; and went away and hanged himself.

verses.name: Matthew 27:6
verses.text: The chief priests took the pieces of silver, but they said: “We must not put them into the Temple treasury, because they are blood-money.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:7
verses.text: So, after consultation, they bought with them the ‘Potter’s Field’ for a burial-ground for foreigners;

verses.name: Matthew 27:8
verses.text: and that is why that field is called the ‘Field of Blood’ to this very day.

verses.name: Matthew 27:9
verses.text: Then it was that these words spoken by the prophet Jeremiah were fulfilled — ‘They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him who was valued, whom some of the people of Israel valued,

verses.name: Matthew 27:10
verses.text: and gave them for the Potter’s field, as the Lord commanded me.’

verses.name: Matthew 27:11
verses.text: Meanwhile Jesus was brought before the Roman Governor. “Are you the king of the Jews?” asked the Governor. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“It is true,” </q>answered Jesus.

verses.name: Matthew 27:12
verses.text: While charges were being brought against him by the chief priests and councillors, Jesus made no reply.

verses.name: Matthew 27:13
verses.text: Then Pilate said to him: “Do not you hear how many accusations they are making against you?”

verses.name: Matthew 27:14
verses.text: Yet Jesus made no reply — not even a single word; at which the Governor was greatly astonished.

verses.name: Matthew 27:15
verses.text: Now, at the feast, the Governor was accustomed to grant the people the release of any one prisoner whom they might choose.

verses.name: Matthew 27:16
verses.text: At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Barabbas.

verses.name: Matthew 27:17
verses.text: So, when the people had collected, Pilate said to them: “Which do you wish me to release for you? Barabbas? Or Jesus who is called ‘Christ’?”

verses.name: Matthew 27:18
verses.text: For he knew that it was out of jealousy that they had given Jesus up to him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:19
verses.text: While he was still on the Bench, his wife sent this message to him — “Do not have anything to do with that good man, for I have been very unhappy today in a dream because of him.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:20
verses.text: But the chief priests and the councillors persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas, and to kill Jesus.

verses.name: Matthew 27:21
verses.text: The Governor, however, said to them: “Which of these two do you wish me to release for you?” <div sID="gen7054" type="paragraph"/> “Barabbas,” they answered.

verses.name: Matthew 27:22
verses.text: “What then,” Pilate asked, “should I do with Jesus who is called ‘Christ?’ “Let him be crucified,” they all replied.

verses.name: Matthew 27:23
verses.text: “Why, what harm has he done?” he asked. But they kept shouting furiously: “Let him be crucified!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:24
verses.text: When Pilate saw that his efforts were unavailing, but that, on the contrary, a riot was beginning, he took some water, and washed his hands in the sight of the crowd, saying as he did so: “I am not answerable for this bloodshed; you must see to it yourselves.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:25
verses.text: And all the people answered: “His blood be on our heads and on our children’s!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:26
verses.text: The Pilate released Barabbas to them; but Jesus he scourged, and gave him up to be crucified.  <div eID="gen7054" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv293"/><div sID="gen7055" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv293"/> After that, the Governor’s soldiers took Jesus with them into the Government house, and gathered the whole garrison around him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:28
verses.text: They stripped him, and put on him a red military cloak,

verses.name: Matthew 27:29
verses.text: and having twisted some thorns into a crown, put it on his head, and a rod in his right hand, and then, going down on their knees before him, they mocked him. “Long life to you, king of the Jews!” they said.

verses.name: Matthew 27:30
verses.text: They spat at him and, taking the rod, kept striking him on the head;

verses.name: Matthew 27:31
verses.text: and, when they had left off mocking him, they took off the military cloak, and put his own clothes on him, and led him away to be crucified.  <div eID="gen7055" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv294"/><div sID="gen7056" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv294"/> As they were on their way out, they came upon a man from Cyrene of the name of Simon; and they compelled him to go with them to carry the cross.

verses.name: Matthew 27:33
verses.text: On reaching a place named Golgotha (a place named from its likeness to a skull),

verses.name: Matthew 27:34
verses.text: they gave him some wine to drink which had been mixed with gall; but after tasting it, Jesus refused to drink it.

verses.name: Matthew 27:35
verses.text: When they had crucified him, they divided his clothes among them by casting lots.

verses.name: Matthew 27:36
verses.text: Then they sat down, and kept watch over him there.

verses.name: Matthew 27:37
verses.text: Above his head they fixed the accusation against him written out — ‘THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.’

verses.name: Matthew 27:38
verses.text: At the same time two robbers were crucified with him, one on the right, the other on the left.

verses.name: Matthew 27:39
verses.text: The passers-by railed at him, shaking their heads as they said:

verses.name: Matthew 27:40
verses.text: “You who ‘destroy the Temple and build one in three days,’ save yourself! If you are God’s Son, come down from the cross!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:41
verses.text: In the same way the chief priests, with the Teaches of the law and councillors, said in mockery:

verses.name: Matthew 27:42
verses.text: “He saved others, but he cannot save himself! He is the ‘king of Israel’! Let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:43
verses.text: He has trusted in God; if God wants him, let him deliver him now; for he said ‘I am God’s Son.’”

verses.name: Matthew 27:44
verses.text: Even the robbers, who were crucified with him, insulted him in the same way.

verses.name: Matthew 27:45
verses.text: After midday a darkness came over all the country, lasting until three in the afternoon.

verses.name: Matthew 27:46
verses.text: About three Jesus called out loudly: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Eloi, Eloi, lema sabacthani” </q>— that is to say, <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 27:47
verses.text: Some of those standing by heard this, and said: “The man is calling for Elijah!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:48
verses.text: One of them immediately ran and took a sponge, and, filling it with common wine, put it on the end of a rod, and offered it to him to drink.

verses.name: Matthew 27:49
verses.text: But the rest said: “Wait and let us see if Elijah is coming to save him.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:50
verses.text: But Jesus, uttering another loud cry, gave up his spirit.

verses.name: Matthew 27:51
verses.text: Suddenly the Temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom, the earth shook, the rocks were torn asunder,

verses.name: Matthew 27:52
verses.text: the tombs opened, and the bodies of many of God’s people who had fallen asleep rose,

verses.name: Matthew 27:53
verses.text: and they, leaving their tombs, went, after the resurrection of Jesus, into the Holy City, and appeared to many people.

verses.name: Matthew 27:54
verses.text: The Roman captain, and the men with him who were watching Jesus, on seeing the earthquake and all that was happening, became greatly frightened and exclaimed: “This must indeed have been God’s Son!”

verses.name: Matthew 27:55
verses.text: There were many women there, watching from a distance, who had accompanied Jesus from Galilee and had been attending on him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:56
verses.text: Among them were Mary of Magdala, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.  <div eID="gen7056" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:57
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv295"/><div sID="gen7057" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv295"/> When evening had fallen, there came a rich man belonging to Ramah, named Joseph, who had himself become a disciple of Jesus.

verses.name: Matthew 27:58
verses.text: He went to see Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus. Pilate ordered it to be given him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:59
verses.text: So Joseph took the body, and wrapped it in a clean linen sheet,

verses.name: Matthew 27:60
verses.text: and laid it in his newly made tomb which he had cut in the rock; and, before he left, he rolled a great stone against the entrance of the tomb.

verses.name: Matthew 27:61
verses.text: Mary of Magdala and the other Mary remained behind, sitting in front of the grave.  <div eID="gen7057" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:62
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv296"/><div sID="gen7058" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv296"/> The next day — that is, the day following the Preparation-day — the chief priests and Pharisees came in a body to Pilate, and said:

verses.name: Matthew 27:63
verses.text: “Sir, we remember that, during his lifetime, that impostor said <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘I will rise after three days.’</q>

verses.name: Matthew 27:64
verses.text: So order the tomb to be made secure until the third day. Otherwise his disciples may come and steal him, and then say to the people ‘He has risen from the dead,’ when the latest imposture will be worse than the first.”  <div eID="gen7058" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:65
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv297"/><div sID="gen7059" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv297"/> “You may have a guard,” was Pilate’s reply; “go and make the tomb as secure as you can.”

verses.name: Matthew 27:66
verses.text: So they went made the tomb secure, by sealing the stone, in presence of the guard.  <div eID="gen7059" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Matt.27"/> <div eID="gen7016" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Matthew 28:1
verses.text: After the Sabbath, as the first day of the week began to dawn, Mary of Magdala and the other Mary had gone to look at the grave,

verses.name: Matthew 28:2
verses.text: when suddenly a great earthquake occurred. For an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled away the stone, and seated himself on it.

verses.name: Matthew 28:3
verses.text: His appearance was as dazzling as lightning, and his clothing was as white as snow;

verses.name: Matthew 28:4
verses.text: and, in their terror of him, the men on guard trembled violently and became like dead men.

verses.name: Matthew 28:5
verses.text: But the angel, addressing the women, said; “You need not be afraid. I now that it is Jesus, who was crucified, for whom you are looking.

verses.name: Matthew 28:6
verses.text: He is not here; for he has risen, as he said he would. Come, and see the place where he was lying;

verses.name: Matthew 28:7
verses.text: and then go quickly and say to him disciples ‘He has risen from the dead, and is going before you into Galilee; there you will see him.’ Remember, I have told you.”

verses.name: Matthew 28:8
verses.text: They left the tomb quickly, in awe and great joy, and ran to tell the news to the disciples.

verses.name: Matthew 28:9
verses.text: Suddenly Jesus met them. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Welcome!” </q>he said. The women went up to him, and clasped his feet, bowing to the ground before him. Then Jesus said to them:

verses.name: Matthew 28:10
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers and sisters to set out for Galilee, and they will see me there.” </q>

verses.name: Matthew 28:11
verses.text: While they were still on their way, some of the guard came into the city, and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.

verses.name: Matthew 28:12
verses.text: So they and the councillors met and, after holding a consultation, gave a large sum of money to the soldiers,

verses.name: Matthew 28:13
verses.text: and told them to say that his disciples came in the night, and stole him while they were asleep;

verses.name: Matthew 28:14
verses.text: “And should this matter come before the Governor,” they added, “we will satisfy him, and see that you have nothing to fear.”

verses.name: Matthew 28:15
verses.text: So the soldiers took the money, and did as they were instructed. This story spread widely; the people of Judea still tell it today.

verses.name: Matthew 28:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv298"/><div sID="gen7061" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv298"/> The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus told them to meet him;

verses.name: Matthew 28:17
verses.text: and, when they saw him, they bowed to the ground before him; although some felt doubtful.

verses.name: Matthew 28:18
verses.text: Then Jesus came up, and spoke to them , saying: <div eID="gen7061" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7062" type="paragraph"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“All authority in heaven and on the earth has been given to me.</q>

verses.name: Matthew 28:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the faith of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit,</q>

verses.name: Matthew 28:20
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and teaching them to lay to heart all the commands that I have given you; and, remember, I myself am with you every day until the close of the age.” </q>  <div eID="gen7062" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7060" type="majorSection"/> <chapter eID="Matt.28"/> <div eID="gen6799" osisID="Matt" type="book"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:1
verses.text: The beginning of the good news about Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Mark 1:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv299"/><div sID="gen7065" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv299"/> It is said in the prophet Isaiah — <lg sID="gen7066"/> <l sID="gen7067"/>‘I am sending my messenger ahead of you;<l eID="gen7067"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7068"/>he will prepare your way.<l eID="gen7068" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7069"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:3
verses.text: The voice of one crying aloud in the wilderness:<l eID="gen7069" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7070"/>“Prepare the road for the Lord,<l eID="gen7070" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen7071"/>make a straight path for him.”’<l eID="gen7071" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen7066"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:4
verses.text: John the Baptizer appeared in the wilderness, proclaiming a baptism on repentance, for the forgiveness of sins.

verses.name: Mark 1:5
verses.text: The whole of Judea, as well as all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, went out to him; and they were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.  <div eID="gen7065" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv300"/><div sID="gen7072" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv300"/> John wore clothes made of camels’ hair, with a leather strap around his waist, and lived on locusts and wild honey;

verses.name: Mark 1:7
verses.text: and he proclaimed — “After me is coming someone more powerful than I am, and I am not fit even to stoop down and unfasten his sandals.

verses.name: Mark 1:8
verses.text: I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”  <div eID="gen7072" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv301"/><div sID="gen7073" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv301"/> Now about that time Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

verses.name: Mark 1:10
verses.text: Just as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens split open and the Spirit coming down to him like a dove,

verses.name: Mark 1:11
verses.text: and from the heavens came a voice — “You are my dearly loved son; you bring me great joy.”  <div eID="gen7073" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv302"/><div sID="gen7074" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv302"/> Immediately afterwards the Spirit drove Jesus out into the wilderness;

verses.name: Mark 1:13
verses.text: and he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan, and among the wild beasts, while the angels helped him.  <div eID="gen7074" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7064" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv303"/><div sID="gen7075" type="majorSection"/> <title>The Work in Galilee</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv303"/> After John had been arrested, Jesus went to Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God —

verses.name: Mark 1:15
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The time has come, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent, and believe the good news.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 1:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv304"/><div sID="gen7076" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv304"/> As Jesus was going along the shore of the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew casting a net in the Sea, for they were fishermen.

verses.name: Mark 1:17
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Come and follow me,”</q>Jesus said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“and I will teach you to fish for people.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 1:18
verses.text: They left their nets at once, and followed him.  <div eID="gen7076" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv305"/><div sID="gen7077" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv305"/> Going on a little further, he saw James, Zebedee’s son, and his brother John, who were in their boat mending the nets.

verses.name: Mark 1:20
verses.text: Jesus called them at once, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the crew, and went after him.  <div eID="gen7077" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv306"/><div sID="gen7078" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv306"/> They walked to Capernaum. On the next Sabbath Jesus went into the synagogue and began to teach.

verses.name: Mark 1:22
verses.text: The people were amazed at his teaching, for he taught them like one who had authority, and not like the teachers of the law.

verses.name: Mark 1:23
verses.text: Now there was in their synagogue at the time a man under the power of a foul spirit, who called out:

verses.name: Mark 1:24
verses.text: “What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are — the Holy One of God!”

verses.name: Mark 1:25
verses.text: But Jesus rebuked the spirit: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Be silent! Come out from him.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 1:26
verses.text: The foul spirit threw the man into a fit, and with a loud cry came out from him.

verses.name: Mark 1:27
verses.text: They were all so amazed that they kept asking each other: “What is this? What is this strange teaching? He gives his commands with authority even to the foul spirits, and they obey him!”

verses.name: Mark 1:28
verses.text: His fame spread at once in all directions, through the whole neighborhood of Galilee.  <div eID="gen7078" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv307"/><div sID="gen7079" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv307"/> As soon as they had left the synagogue, they went, with James and John, into the house of Simon and Andrew.

verses.name: Mark 1:30
verses.text: Now Simon’s mother-in-law was lying ill with a fever, and they at once told Jesus about her.

verses.name: Mark 1:31
verses.text: Jesus went up to her and, grasping her hand, raised her up; the fever left her, and she began to take care of them.  <div eID="gen7079" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv308"/><div sID="gen7080" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv308"/> In the evening, after sunset, the people brought to Jesus all who were ill or possessed by demons;

verses.name: Mark 1:33
verses.text: and the whole city was gathered around the door.

verses.name: Mark 1:34
verses.text: Jesus cured many who were ill with various diseases, and drove out many demons, and would not permit them to speak, because they knew him to be the Christ.  <div eID="gen7080" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv309"/><div sID="gen7081" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv309"/> In the morning, long before daylight, Jesus rose and went out, and, going to a lonely spot, there began to pray.

verses.name: Mark 1:36
verses.text: But Simon and his companions went out searching for him;

verses.name: Mark 1:37
verses.text: and, when they found him, they exclaimed: “Everyone is looking for you!”

verses.name: Mark 1:38
verses.text: But Jesus said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Let us go somewhere else, into the country towns nearby so that I can make my proclamation in them also; for that was why I came.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 1:39
verses.text: And he went about making his proclamation in their Synagogues all through Galilee, and driving out the demons.  <div eID="gen7081" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv310"/><div sID="gen7082" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv310"/> One day a leper came to Jesus and, falling on his knees, begged him for help. “If only you are willing,” he said, “you are able to make me clean.”

verses.name: Mark 1:41
verses.text: Moved with compassion, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying as he did so: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I am willing; become clean.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 1:42
verses.text: Instantly the leprosy left the man, and he became clean;

verses.name: Mark 1:43
verses.text: and then Jesus, after sternly warning him, immediately sent him away, and said to him:

verses.name: Mark 1:44
