verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv396"/><div sID="gen7178" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv396"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“You do not know what you are asking,”</q>Jesus said to them. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Can you drink the cup that I am to drink? Or receive the baptism that I am to receive?”</q>  <div eID="gen7178" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv397"/><div sID="gen7179" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv397"/> “Yes,” they answered, “we can.” <div eID="gen7179" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7180" type="paragraph"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“You will indeed drink the cup that I am to drink,”</q>Jesus said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“and receive the baptism that I am to receive,</q>

verses.name: Mark 10:40
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">but as to a seat at my right or at my left — that is not mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”</q>  <div eID="gen7180" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv398"/><div sID="gen7181" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv398"/> On hearing of this, the ten others were at first very indignant about James and John.

verses.name: Mark 10:42
verses.text: But Jesus called the ten to him, and said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Those who are regarded as ruling among the Gentiles lord it over them, as you know, and their great men oppress them.</q>

verses.name: Mark 10:43
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But among you it is not so. No, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,</q>

verses.name: Mark 10:44
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and whoever wants to take the first place among you must be the servant of all;</q>

verses.name: Mark 10:45
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for even the Son of Man came, not be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”</q>  <div eID="gen7181" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv399"/><div sID="gen7182" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv399"/> They came to Jericho. When Jesus was going out of the town with his disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the roadside.

verses.name: Mark 10:47
verses.text: Hearing that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to call out: “Jesus, Son of David, take pity on me.”

verses.name: Mark 10:48
verses.text: Many of the people kept telling him to be quiet; but the man continued to call out all the louder: “Son of David, take pity on me.”

verses.name: Mark 10:49
verses.text: Then Jesus stopped. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Call him,”</q>he said. So they called the blind man. “Courage!” they exclaimed. “Get up; he is calling you.”

verses.name: Mark 10:50
verses.text: The man threw off his cloak, sprang up, and came to Jesus.

verses.name: Mark 10:51
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“What do you want me to do for you?”</q>said Jesus, addressing him. “Rabboni,” the blind man answered, “I want to recover my sight.”  <div eID="gen7182" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:52
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv400"/><div sID="gen7183" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv400"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“You may go,”</q>Jesus said; <q marker="" who="Jesus">“your faith has delivered you.”</q>Immediately he recovered his sight, and began to follow Jesus along the road.  <div eID="gen7183" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7175" type="section"/> <chapter eID="Mark.10"/> <div eID="gen7163" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:1
verses.text: When they had almost reached Jerusalem, as far as Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent on two of his disciples.

verses.name: Mark 11:2
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Go to the village facing you,”</q>he said; <q marker="" who="Jesus">“and, as soon as you get there, you will find a foal tethered, which no one has ever ridden; untie it, and bring it.</q>

verses.name: Mark 11:3
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And, if anyone says to you ‘Why are you doing that?’, say ‘The Master wants it, and will be sure to send it back here at once.’”</q>

verses.name: Mark 11:4
verses.text: The two disciples went, and, finding a foal tethered outside a door in the street, they untied it.

verses.name: Mark 11:5
verses.text: Some of the bystanders said to them: “What are you doing, untying the foal?”

verses.name: Mark 11:6
verses.text: And the two disciples answered as Jesus had told them; and they allowed them to go.

verses.name: Mark 11:7
verses.text: Then they brought the foal to Jesus, and, when they had laid their cloaks on it, he seated himself on it.

verses.name: Mark 11:8
verses.text: Many of the people spread their cloaks on the road, while some strewed boughs which they had cut from the fields;

verses.name: Mark 11:9
verses.text: and those who led the way, as well as those who followed, kept shouting: “‘God save him! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!’

verses.name: Mark 11:10
verses.text: Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! ‘God save him from on high!’”

verses.name: Mark 11:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv401"/><div sID="gen7185" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv401"/> Jesus entered Jerusalem, and went into the Temple Courts; and, after looking around at everything, as it was already late, he went out to Bethany with the Twelve.  <div eID="gen7185" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv402"/><div sID="gen7186" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv402"/> The next day, after they had left Bethany, Jesus became hungry;

verses.name: Mark 11:13
verses.text: and, noticing a fig-tree at a distance in leaf, he went to it to see if by any chance he could find something on it; but, on coming up to it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.

verses.name: Mark 11:14
verses.text: So, addressing the tree, he exclaimed: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“May no one ever again eat of your fruit!”</q>And his disciples heard what he said.  <div eID="gen7186" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv403"/><div sID="gen7187" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv403"/> They came to Jerusalem. Jesus went into the Temple Courts, and began to drive out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers, and the seats of the pigeon-dealers,

verses.name: Mark 11:16
verses.text: and would not allow anyone to carry anything across the Temple Courts.

verses.name: Mark 11:17
verses.text: Then he began to teach. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Does not scripture say,”</q>he asked, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.’”</q>

verses.name: Mark 11:18
verses.text: Now the chief priests and the teachers of the law heard this and began to look for some way of putting Jesus to death; for they were afraid of him, since all the people were greatly impressed by his teaching.

verses.name: Mark 11:19
verses.text: As soon as evening fell, Jesus and his disciples went out of the city.  <div eID="gen7187" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv404"/><div sID="gen7188" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv404"/> As they passed by early in the morning, they noticed that the fig-tree was withered up from the roots.

verses.name: Mark 11:21
verses.text: Then Peter recalled what had occurred. “Look, Rabbi,” he exclaimed, “the fig-tree which you doomed is withered up!”  <div eID="gen7188" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv405"/><div sID="gen7189" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv405"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Have faith in God!”</q>replied Jesus.

verses.name: Mark 11:23
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you that if anyone should say to this hill ‘Be lifted up and hurled into the sea!’, without ever a doubt in his mind, but in the faith that what he says will be done, he would find that it would be.</q>

verses.name: Mark 11:24
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And therefore I say to you ‘Have faith that whatever you ask for in prayer is already granted you, and you will find that it will be.’</q>  <div eID="gen7189" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv406"/><div sID="gen7190" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv406"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘And, whenever you stand up to pray, forgive any grievance that you have against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven also may forgive you your offenses.”</q>  <div eID="gen7190" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 11:27
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv407"/><div sID="gen7191" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv407"/> They came to Jerusalem again. While Jesus was walking about in the Temple Courts, the chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the councillors came up to him.

verses.name: Mark 11:28
verses.text: “What authority have you to do these things?” they said. “Who gave you the authority to do them?”

verses.name: Mark 11:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv408"/><div sID="gen7192" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv408"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I will put one question to you,”</q>said Jesus. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Answer me that, and then I will tell you what authority I have to act as I do.</q>

verses.name: Mark 11:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">It is about John’s baptism. Was it of divine or human origin? Answer me that.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 11:31
verses.text: They began arguing together; “If we say ‘divine,’ he will say ‘Why then did not you believe him?’

verses.name: Mark 11:32
verses.text: Yet can we say ‘human’?” — They were afraid of the people, for everyone regarded John as undoubtedly a prophet.

verses.name: Mark 11:33
verses.text: So their answer to Jesus was — “We do not know.” <div eID="gen7192" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7193" type="paragraph"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Then I,”</q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“refuse to tell you what authority I have to do these things.”</q>  <div eID="gen7193" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv409"/><div sID="gen7194" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7194" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Mark.11"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:1
verses.text: Jesus began to speak to them in parables: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“A man once planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a wine-press, built a tower, and then let it out to tenants and went abroad.</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:2
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">At the proper time he sent a servant to the tenants, to receive from them a share of the produce of the grape harvest;</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:3
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">but they seized him, and beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:4
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">A second time the owner sent a servant to them; this man, too, the tenants struck on the head, and insulted.</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:5
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">He sent another, but him they killed; and so with many others — some they beat and some they killed.</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">He had still one son, who was very dear to him; and him he sent to them last of all. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But those tenants said to one another ‘Here is the heir! Come, let us kill him, and his inheritance will be ours.’</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">So they seized him, and killed him, and threw his body outside the vineyard.</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and put the tenants to death, and he will let the vineyard to others.</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv409"/><div sID="gen7195" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv409"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘Have you never read this passage of scripture? — ‘The stone which the builders despised has now itself become the corner-stone;</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">this corner-stone has come from the Lord, and is marvelous in our eyes.’”</q>  <div eID="gen7195" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv410"/><div sID="gen7196" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv410"/> After this his enemies were eager to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowd; for they saw that it was at them that he had aimed the parable. So they let him alone, and went away.  <div eID="gen7196" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7191" type="section"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv411"/><div sID="gen7197" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv411"/> Afterwards they sent to Jesus some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to set a trap for him in the course of conversation.

verses.name: Mark 12:14
verses.text: These men came to him and said: “Teacher, we know that you are an honest man, and are not afraid of anyone, for you pay no regard to a person’s position, but teach the way of God honestly; are we right in paying taxes to the Emperor, or not?

verses.name: Mark 12:15
verses.text: Should we pay, or should we not pay?” Knowing their hypocrisy, Jesus said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Why are you testing me? Bring me a coin to look at.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:16
verses.text: And, when they had brought it, he asked: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Whose head and title are these?”</q> <div sID="gen7198" type="paragraph"/> “The Emperor’s,” they said;

verses.name: Mark 12:17
verses.text: and Jesus replied: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Pay to the Emperor what belongs to the Emperor, and to God what belongs to God.”</q>And they wondered at him.  <div eID="gen7198" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv412"/><div sID="gen7199" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv412"/> Next came some Sadducees — the men who maintain that there is no resurrection. Their question was this —

verses.name: Mark 12:19
verses.text: “Teacher, in our scriptures Moses decreed that, should a man’s brother die, leaving a widow but no child, the man should take the widow as his wife, and raise up a family for his brother.

verses.name: Mark 12:20
verses.text: There were once seven brothers; of whom the eldest took a wife, but died and left no family;

verses.name: Mark 12:21
verses.text: and the second took her, and died without family; and so did the third.

verses.name: Mark 12:22
verses.text: All the seven died and left no family. The woman herself died last of all.

verses.name: Mark 12:23
verses.text: At the resurrection whose wife will she be, all seven brothers having had her as their wife?”  <div eID="gen7199" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv413"/><div sID="gen7200" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv413"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Is not the reason of your mistake,”</q>answered Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“your ignorance of the scriptures and of the power of God?</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">When people rise from the dead, there is no marrying or being married; but they are as angels in heaven.</q>  <div eID="gen7200" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv414"/><div sID="gen7201" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv414"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“As to the dead, and the fact that they rise, have you never read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the Bush, how God spoke to him saying — ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">He is not God of dead people, but of living. You are greatly mistaken.”</q>  <div eID="gen7201" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv415"/><div sID="gen7202" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv415"/> Then came up one of the teachers of the law who had heard their discussions. Knowing that Jesus had answered them wisely, he asked him this question: “What is the first of all the commandments?”  <div eID="gen7202" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv416"/><div sID="gen7203" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv416"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“The first,”</q>answered Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“is — ‘Hear, Israel; the Lord our God is the one Lord;</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and you must love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:31
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The second is this — ‘You must love your neighbor as you love yourself.’ There is no commandment greater than these.”</q>  <div eID="gen7203" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv417"/><div sID="gen7204" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv417"/> “Wisely answered, teacher!” exclaimed the teacher of the law. “It is true, as you say, that ‘there is one God,’ and that ‘there is no other besides him’;

verses.name: Mark 12:33
verses.text: and to ‘love him with all one’s heart, and with all one’s understanding, and with all one’s strength,’ and to ‘love one’s neighbor as one loves oneself’ is far beyond all ‘burnt offerings and sacrifices.’”

verses.name: Mark 12:34
verses.text: Seeing that he had answered with discernment, Jesus said to him: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“You are not far from the kingdom of God.”</q> <div eID="gen7204" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7205" type="paragraph"/> After that no one ventured to question him further.  <div eID="gen7205" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv418"/><div sID="gen7206" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv418"/> While Jesus was teaching in the Temple Courts, he asked: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“How is it that the teachers of the law say that the Christ is to be David’s son?</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:36
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">David said himself, speaking under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit — ‘The Lord said to my lord: “Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies beneath your feet.’”</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:37
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">David himself calls him ‘lord,’ how comes it, then, that he is to be his son?”</q> <div eID="gen7206" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7207" type="paragraph"/> The mass of the people listened to Jesus with delight.

verses.name: Mark 12:38
verses.text: In the course of his teaching, Jesus said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“See that you are on your guard against the teachers of the law, who delight to walk about in long robes, and to be greeted in the streets with respect,</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:39
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and to have the best seats in the Synagogues, and places of honor at dinner.</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:40
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">They are the men who rob widows of their homes, and make a pretense of saying long prayers. Their sentence will be all the heavier.”</q>  <div eID="gen7207" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 12:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv419"/><div sID="gen7208" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv419"/> Then Jesus sat down opposite the chests for the Temple offerings, and watched how the people put money into them. Many rich people were putting in large sums;

verses.name: Mark 12:42
verses.text: but one poor widow came and put in two small coins, worth very little.

verses.name: Mark 12:43
verses.text: Then, calling his disciples to him, Jesus said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you that this poor widow has put in more than all the others who were putting money into the chests;</q>

verses.name: Mark 12:44
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for everyone else put in something from what he had to spare, while she, in her need, put in all she had — everything that she had to live on.”</q>  <div eID="gen7208" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Mark.12"/> <div eID="gen7197" type="section"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv420"/><div sID="gen7209" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv420"/> As Jesus was walking out of the Temple Courts, one of his disciples said to him: “Teacher, look what fine stones and buildings these are!”

verses.name: Mark 13:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv421"/><div sID="gen7210" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv421"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Do you see these great buildings?”</q>asked Jesus. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Not a single stone will be left here on another, which will not be thrown down.”</q>  <div eID="gen7210" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv422"/><div sID="gen7211" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv422"/> When Jesus had sat down on the Mount of Olives, facing the Temple, Peter, James, John and Andrew questioned him privately:

verses.name: Mark 13:4
verses.text: “Tell us when this will be, and what will be the sign when all this is drawing to its close.”  <div eID="gen7211" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv423"/><div sID="gen7212" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv423"/> Then Jesus began: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“See that no one leads you astray.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:6
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Many will take my name, and come saying ‘I am He’, and will lead many astray.</q>  <div eID="gen7212" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv424"/><div sID="gen7213" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv424"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“And, when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed; such things must occur; but the end is not yet.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For ‘nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom’; there will be earthquakes in various places; there will be famines. This will be but the beginning of the birth-pangs.</q>  <div eID="gen7213" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv425"/><div sID="gen7214" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv425"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“See to yourselves! They will betray you to courts of law; and you will be taken to Synagogues and beaten; and you will be brought up before governors and kings for my sake, so that you can bear witness before them.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:10
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But the good news must first be proclaimed to every nation.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:11
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Whenever they betray you and hand you over for trial, do not be anxious beforehand as to what you will say, but say whatever is given you at the moment; for it will not be you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:12
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Brother will betray brother to death, and the father his child; and children will turn against their parents, and cause them to be put to death;</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:13
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and you will be hated by everyone because of me. Yet the person who endures to the end will be saved.</q>  <div eID="gen7214" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv426"/><div sID="gen7215" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv426"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“As soon, however, as you see ‘the Foul Desecration’ standing where he ought not”</q>(the reader must consider what this means) <q marker="" who="Jesus">“then those of you who are in Judea must take refuge in the mountains;</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:15
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and a person on the house-top must not go down, or go in to get anything out of their house:</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:16
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">nor must one who is on their farm turn back to get their cloak.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:17
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And alas for pregnant women, and for those who are nursing infants in those days!</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:18
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Pray, too, that this may not occur in winter.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:19
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">For those days will be a time of distress, the like of which has not occurred from the beginning of God’s creation until now — and never will again.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:20
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And, had not the Lord put a limit to those days, not a single soul would escape; but, for the sake of God’s own chosen people, he did limit them.</q>  <div eID="gen7215" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv427"/><div sID="gen7216" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv427"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“And at that time if anyone should say to you ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ ‘Look, there he is!’, do not believe it;</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:22
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">for false Christs and false prophets will arise, and display signs and marvels, to lead astray, were it possible, even God’s people.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:23
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">But see that you are on your guard! I have told you all this beforehand.</q>  <div eID="gen7216" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:24
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv428"/><div sID="gen7217" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv428"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“In those days, after that time of distress, ‘the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give her light,</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">the stars will be falling from the heavens,’ and ‘the forces that are in the heavens will be convulsed.’</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:26
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Then will be seen the ‘Son of Man coming in clouds’ with great power and glory;</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:27
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and then he will send the angels, and gather his people from the four winds, from one end of the world to the other.</q>  <div eID="gen7217" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv429"/><div sID="gen7218" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv429"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Learn the lesson taught by the fig-tree. As soon as its branches are full of sap, and it is bursting into leaf, you know that summer is near.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:29
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And so may you, as soon as you see these things happening, know that he is at your doors.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:30
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I tell you that even the present generation will not pass away, until all these things have taken place.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:31
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">The heavens and the earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.</q>  <div eID="gen7218" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv430"/><div sID="gen7219" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv430"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“But about ‘that day,’ or ‘the hour,’ no one knows — not even the angels in heaven, not even the Son — but only the Father.</q>  <div eID="gen7219" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 13:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv431"/><div sID="gen7220" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv431"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“See that you are on the watch; for you do not know when the time will be.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:34
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">It is like a man going on a journey, who leaves his home, puts his servants in charge — each having their special duty — and orders the porter to watch.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:35
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Therefore watch, for you cannot be sure when the Master of the house is coming — whether in the evening, at midnight, at daybreak, or in the morning — </q>

verses.name: Mark 13:36
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">otherwise he might come suddenly and find you asleep.</q>

verses.name: Mark 13:37
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And what I say to you I say to all — Watch!”</q>  <div eID="gen7220" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Mark.13"/> <div eID="gen7209" type="section"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv432"/><div sID="gen7221" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv432"/> It was now two days before the Festival of the Passover and the unleavened bread. The chief priests and the teachers of the law were looking for an opportunity to arrest Jesus by stealth, and to put him to death;

verses.name: Mark 14:2
verses.text: for they said: “Not during the Festival, or the people may riot.”

verses.name: Mark 14:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv433"/><div sID="gen7222" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv433"/> When Jesus was still at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, while he was sitting at the table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of choice spikenard perfume of great value. She broke the jar, and poured the perfume on his head.

verses.name: Mark 14:4
verses.text: Some of those who were present said to one another indignantly: “Why has the perfume been wasted like this?

verses.name: Mark 14:5
verses.text: This perfume could have been sold for more than a year's wages, and the money given to the poor.”  <div eID="gen7222" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv434"/><div sID="gen7223" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv434"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Leave her alone,”</q>said Jesus, as they began to find fault with her, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“why are you troubling her? This is a beautiful deed that she has done for me.</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:7
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">You always have the poor with you, and whenever you wish you can do good to them; but you will not always have me.</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:8
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">She has done what she could; she has perfumed my body beforehand for my burial.</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:9
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">And I tell you, wherever, in the whole world, the good news is proclaimed, what this woman has done will be told in memory of her.”</q>  <div eID="gen7223" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv435"/><div sID="gen7224" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv435"/> After this, Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests, to betray Jesus to them.

verses.name: Mark 14:11
verses.text: They were glad to hear what he said, and promised to pay him. So he began looking for a good opportunity to betray Jesus.  <div eID="gen7224" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7221" type="section"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv436"/><div sID="gen7225" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv436"/> On the first day of the Festival of the unleavened bread, when it was customary to kill the Passover lambs, his disciples said to Jesus: “Where do you wish us to go and make preparations for your eating the Passover?”

verses.name: Mark 14:13
verses.text: Jesus sent forward two of his disciples and said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Go into the city, and there a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you; follow him;</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:14
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">and, wherever he goes in, say to the owner of the house ‘The teacher says — Where is my room where I am to eat the Passover with my disciples?’</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:15
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">He will himself show you a large upstairs room, set out ready; and there make preparations for us.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:16
verses.text: So the disciples set out and went into the city, and found everything just as Jesus had told them; and they prepared the Passover.

verses.name: Mark 14:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv437"/><div sID="gen7226" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv437"/> In the evening he went there with the Twelve,

verses.name: Mark 14:18
verses.text: and when they had taken their places and were eating, Jesus said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you that one of you is going to betray me — one who is eating with me.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:19
verses.text: They were grieved at this, and began to say to him, one after another: “Can it be I?”  <div eID="gen7226" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv438"/><div sID="gen7227" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv438"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“It is one of you Twelve,”</q>said Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“the one who is dipping his bread beside me into the dish.</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:21
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">True, the Son of Man must go, as scripture says of him, yet alas for that man by whom the Son of Man is being betrayed! For that man ‘it would be better never to have been born!’”</q>  <div eID="gen7227" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv439"/><div sID="gen7228" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv439"/> While they were eating, Jesus took some bread, and, after saying the blessing, broke it, and gave it to them, and said: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Take it; this is my body.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:23
verses.text: Then he took a cup, and, after saying the thanksgiving, gave it to them, and they all drank from it.

verses.name: Mark 14:24
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“This is my covenant-blood,”</q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“which is poured out on behalf of many.</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:25
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I tell you that I will never again drink of the juice of the grape, until that day when I will drink it new in the kingdom of God.”</q>  <div eID="gen7228" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv440"/><div sID="gen7229" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv440"/> They then sang a hymn, and went out up the Mount of Olives,

verses.name: Mark 14:27
verses.text: presently Jesus said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“All of you will fall away; for scripture says — ‘I will strike down the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:28
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Yet, after I have risen, I will go before you into Galilee.”</q>  <div eID="gen7229" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv441"/><div sID="gen7230" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv441"/> “Even if everyone else falls away,” said Peter, “yet I will not.”  <div eID="gen7230" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:30
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv442"/><div sID="gen7231" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv442"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I tell you,”</q>answered Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“that you yourself today — yes, this very night — before the cock crows twice, will disown me three times.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:31
verses.text: But Peter vehemently protested: “Even if I must die with you, I will never disown you!” And they all said the same.  <div eID="gen7231" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7225" type="section"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:32
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv443"/><div sID="gen7232" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv443"/> Presently they came to a garden known as Gethsemane, and Jesus said to his disciples <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Sit down here while I pray.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:33
verses.text: He took with him Peter, James, and John; and began to show signs of great dismay and deep distress of mind.

verses.name: Mark 14:34
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I am sad at heart,”</q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“sad even to death; wait here, and watch.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:35
verses.text: Going on a little further, he threw himself on the ground, and began to pray that, if it were possible, he might be spared that hour.

verses.name: Mark 14:36
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Abba, Father,”</q>he said, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“all things are possible to you; take away this cup from me; yet, not what I will, but what you will.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:37
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv444"/><div sID="gen7233" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv444"/> Then he came and found the three apostles asleep. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Simon,”</q>he said to Peter, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“are you asleep? Could not you watch for one hour?</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:38
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Watch and pray,” he said to them all, “so that you may not fall into temptation. True, the spirit is eager, but human nature is weak.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:39
verses.text: Again he went away, and prayed in the same words;

verses.name: Mark 14:40
verses.text: and coming back again he found them asleep, for their eyes were heavy; and they did not know what to say to him.  <div eID="gen7233" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:41
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv445"/><div sID="gen7234" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv445"/> A third time he came, and said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Sleep on now, and rest yourselves. Enough! My time has come. Look: the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of wicked people.</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:42
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Up, and let us be going. Look! My betrayer is close at hand.”</q>  <div eID="gen7234" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:43
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv446"/><div sID="gen7235" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv446"/> And just then, while he was still speaking, Judas, who was one of the Twelve, came up; and with him a crowd of people, with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the councillors.

verses.name: Mark 14:44
verses.text: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them. “The man whom I kiss,” he had said, “will be the one; arrest him and take him away safely.”

verses.name: Mark 14:45
verses.text: As soon as Judas came, he went up to Jesus at once, and said: “Rabbi!” and kissed him.

verses.name: Mark 14:46
verses.text: Then the men seized Jesus, and arrested him.  <div eID="gen7235" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:47
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv447"/><div sID="gen7236" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv447"/> One of those who were standing by drew his sword, and struck at the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.

verses.name: Mark 14:48
verses.text: But Jesus spoke up, and said to the men: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Have you come out, as if after a robber, with swords and clubs, to take me? </q>

verses.name: Mark 14:49
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">I have been among you day after day in the Temple Courts teaching, and yet you did not arrest me; but this is in fulfillment of the scriptures.” </q>

verses.name: Mark 14:50
verses.text: And all the apostles forsook him, and fled.

verses.name: Mark 14:51
verses.text: One young man did indeed follow him, wrapped only in a linen sheet. They tried to arrest him;

verses.name: Mark 14:52
verses.text: but he left the sheet in their hands, and fled naked.  <div eID="gen7236" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7232" type="section"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:53
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv448"/><div sID="gen7237" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv448"/> Then they took Jesus to the high priest; and all the chief priests, the councillors, and the teachers of the law assembled.

verses.name: Mark 14:54
verses.text: Peter, who had followed Jesus at a distance into the courtyard of the high priest, was sitting there among the police officers, warming himself at the blaze of the fire.

verses.name: Mark 14:55
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv449"/><div sID="gen7238" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv449"/> Meanwhile the chief priest and the whole of the High Council were trying to get such evidence against Jesus as would warrant his being put to death, but they could not find any;

verses.name: Mark 14:56
verses.text: for, though there were many who gave false evidence against him, yet their evidence did not agree.

verses.name: Mark 14:57
verses.text: Presently some men stood up, and gave this false evidence against him —

verses.name: Mark 14:58
verses.text: “We ourselves heard him say ‘I will destroy this Temple made with hands, and in three days build another made without hands.’”

verses.name: Mark 14:59
verses.text: Yet not even on that point did their evidence agree.  <div eID="gen7238" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:60
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv450"/><div sID="gen7239" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv450"/> Then the high priest stood forward, and questioned Jesus. “Have you no answer to make?” he asked. “What is this evidence which these men are giving against you?”

verses.name: Mark 14:61
verses.text: But Jesus remained silent, and made no answer. <div eID="gen7239" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7240" type="paragraph"/> A second time the high priest questioned him. “Are you,” he asked, “the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”  <div eID="gen7240" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:62
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv451"/><div sID="gen7241" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv451"/> <q marker="" who="Jesus">“I am,”</q>replied Jesus, <q marker="" who="Jesus">“and you will all see the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of the Almighty; and ‘coming in the clouds of heaven’.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 14:63
verses.text: At this the high priest tore his vestments. “Why do we want any more witnesses?” he exclaimed.

verses.name: Mark 14:64
verses.text: “You heard his blasphemy? What is your verdict?” They all condemned him, declaring that he deserved death.  <div eID="gen7241" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:65
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv452"/><div sID="gen7242" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv452"/> Some of those present began to spit at him, and to blindfold his eyes, and strike him, saying, as they did so, “Now play the prophet!” and even the police officers received him with blows.  <div eID="gen7242" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 14:66
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv453"/><div sID="gen7243" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv453"/> While Peter was in the courtyard down below, one of the high priest’s maidservants came up;

verses.name: Mark 14:67
verses.text: and, seeing Peter warming himself, she looked closely at him, and exclaimed: “Why, you were with Jesus, the Nazarene!”

verses.name: Mark 14:68
verses.text: But Peter denied it. “I do not know or understand what you mean,” he replied. Then he went out into the porch;

verses.name: Mark 14:69
verses.text: and there the maidservant, on seeing him, began to say again to the bystanders: “This is one of them!”

verses.name: Mark 14:70
verses.text: But Peter again denied it. <div eID="gen7243" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen7244" type="paragraph"/> Soon afterwards the bystanders again said to him: “You certainly are one of them; why you are a Galilean!”

verses.name: Mark 14:71
verses.text: But he said to them: “I swear that I do not know the man you are talking about! May God punish me if I am lying!”

verses.name: Mark 14:72
verses.text: At that moment, for the second time, a cock crowed; and Peter remembered the words that Jesus had said to him — <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘Before a cock has crowed twice, you will disown me three times’;</q>and, as he thought of it, he began to weep.  <div eID="gen7244" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Mark.14"/> <div eID="gen7237" type="section"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv454"/><div sID="gen7245" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv454"/> As soon as it was daylight, the chief priests, after holding a consultation with the councillors and teachers of the law — that is to say, the whole High Council — put Jesus in chains, and took him away, and gave him up to Pilate.

verses.name: Mark 15:2
verses.text: “Are you the king of the Jews?” asked Pilate. <q marker="" who="Jesus">“It is true,”</q>replied Jesus.

verses.name: Mark 15:3
verses.text: Then the chief priests brought a number of charges against him.

verses.name: Mark 15:4
verses.text: So Pilate questioned Jesus again. “Have you no reply to make?” he asked. “Listen, how many charges they are bringing against you.”

verses.name: Mark 15:5
verses.text: But Jesus still made no reply whatever; at which Pilate was astonished.

verses.name: Mark 15:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv455"/><div sID="gen7246" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv455"/> Now, at the feast, Pilate used to grant the people the release of any one prisoner whom they might ask for.

verses.name: Mark 15:7
verses.text: A man called Barabbas was in prison, with the rioters who had committed murder during a riot.

verses.name: Mark 15:8
verses.text: So, when the crowd went up and began to ask Pilate to follow his usual custom,

verses.name: Mark 15:9
verses.text: he answered: “Do you want me to release the ‘king of the Jews’ for you?”

verses.name: Mark 15:10
verses.text: For he was aware that it was out of jealousy that the chief priests had given Jesus up to him.

verses.name: Mark 15:11
verses.text: But the chief priests incited the crowd to get Barabbas released instead.

verses.name: Mark 15:12
verses.text: Pilate, however, spoke to them again: “What should I do then with the man whom you call the ‘king of the Jews’?”

verses.name: Mark 15:13
verses.text: Again they shouted: “Crucify him!”  <div eID="gen7246" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv456"/><div sID="gen7247" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv456"/> “Why, what harm has he done?” Pilate kept saying to them. But they shouted furiously: “Crucify him!”

verses.name: Mark 15:15
verses.text: And Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas to them, and, after scourging Jesus, gave him up to be crucified.  <div eID="gen7247" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:16
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv457"/><div sID="gen7248" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv457"/> The soldiers then took Jesus away into the courtyard — that is the Government house — and they called the whole garrison together.

verses.name: Mark 15:17
verses.text: They dressed him in a purple robe, and, having twisted a crown of thorns, put it on him,

verses.name: Mark 15:18
verses.text: and then began to salute him. “Long life to you, king of the Jews!” they said.

verses.name: Mark 15:19
verses.text: And they kept striking him on the head with a rod, spitting at him, and bowing to the ground before him — going down on their knees;

verses.name: Mark 15:20
verses.text: and, when they had left off mocking him, they took off the purple robe, and put his own clothes on him.  <div eID="gen7248" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7245" type="section"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv458"/><div sID="gen7249" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv458"/> They led Jesus out to crucify him; and they compelled a passer-by, Simon from Cyrene, who was on his way in from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go with them to carry his cross.

verses.name: Mark 15:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv459"/><div sID="gen7250" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv459"/> They brought Jesus to the place which was known as Golgotha — a name which means ‘place of a Skull.’

verses.name: Mark 15:23
verses.text: There they offered him drugged wine; but Jesus refused it.

verses.name: Mark 15:24
verses.text: Then they crucified him, and divided his clothes among them, casting lots for them, to settle what each should take.  <div eID="gen7250" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv460"/><div sID="gen7251" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv460"/> It was nine in the morning when they crucified him.

verses.name: Mark 15:26
verses.text: The words of the charge against him, written up over his head, read — ‘THE KING OF THE JEWS.’

verses.name: Mark 15:27
verses.text: And with him they crucified two robbers, one on the right, and the other on the left.  <div eID="gen7251" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv461"/><div sID="gen7252" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv461"/> The passers-by railed at him, shaking their heads, as they said: “Ah! You who would destroy the Temple and build one in three days,

verses.name: Mark 15:30
verses.text: come down from the cross and save yourself!”

verses.name: Mark 15:31
verses.text: In the same way the chief priests, with the teachers of the law, said to one another in mockery:

verses.name: Mark 15:32
verses.text: “He saved others, but he cannot save himself! Let the Christ, the ‘king of Israel,’ come down from the cross now so that we can see it and believe.” Even the men who had been crucified with Jesus insulted him.  <div eID="gen7252" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:33
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv462"/><div sID="gen7253" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv462"/> At midday, a darkness came over the whole country, lasting until three in the afternoon.

verses.name: Mark 15:34
verses.text: And, at three, Jesus called out loudly: <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘Eloi, Eloi, lama sabacthani?’”</q>which means <q marker="" who="Jesus">‘My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?’</q>

verses.name: Mark 15:35
verses.text: Some of those standing around heard this, and said: “Listen! He is calling for Elijah!”

verses.name: Mark 15:36
verses.text: And a man ran, and, soaking a sponge in common wine, put it on the end of a rod, and offered it to him to drink, saying as he did so: “Wait and let us see if Elijah is coming to take him down.”

verses.name: Mark 15:37
verses.text: But Jesus, giving a loud cry, expired.

verses.name: Mark 15:38
verses.text: The Temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom.

verses.name: Mark 15:39
verses.text: The Roman officer, who was standing facing Jesus, on seeing the way in which he expired, exclaimed: “This man must indeed have been ‘God’s Son’!”  <div eID="gen7253" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7249" type="section"/>

verses.name: Mark 15:40
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv463"/><div sID="gen7254" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv463"/> There were some women also watching from a distance, among them being Mary of Magdala, Mary the mother of James the Little and of Joseph, and Salome —

verses.name: Mark 15:41
verses.text: all of whom used to accompany Jesus when he was in Galilee, and attend on him — besides many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Mark 15:42
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv464"/><div sID="gen7255" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv464"/> The evening had already fallen, when, as it was the Preparation day — the day before the Sabbath —

verses.name: Mark 15:43
verses.text: Joseph from Ramah, a Councillor of good position, who was himself living in expectation of the kingdom of God, came and ventured to go in to see Pilate, and to ask for the body of Jesus.

verses.name: Mark 15:44
verses.text: But Pilate was surprised to hear that he had already died. So he sent for the officer, and asked if he were already dead;

verses.name: Mark 15:45
verses.text: and, on learning from the officer that it was so, he gave the corpse to Joseph.

verses.name: Mark 15:46
verses.text: Joseph, having bought a linen sheet, took Jesus down, and wound the sheet around him, and laid him in a tomb which had been cut out of the rock; and then rolled a stone up against the entrance of the tomb.

verses.name: Mark 15:47
verses.text: Mary of Magdala and Mary, the mother of Joseph, were watching to see where he was laid.  <div eID="gen7255" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7254" type="section"/> <chapter eID="Mark.15"/> <div eID="gen7184" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Mark 16:1
verses.text: When the Sabbath was over, Mary of Magdala, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought some spices, so that they might go and anoint the body of Jesus.

verses.name: Mark 16:2
verses.text: And very early on the first day of the week they went to the tomb, after sunrise.

verses.name: Mark 16:3
verses.text: They were saying to one another: “Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb?”

verses.name: Mark 16:4
verses.text: But, on looking up, they saw that the stone had already been rolled back; it was a very large one.

verses.name: Mark 16:5
verses.text: Going into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on their right, in a white robe, and they were dismayed; But he said to them:

verses.name: Mark 16:6
verses.text: “Do not be dismayed; you are looking for Jesus, the Nazarene, who has been crucified; he has risen, he is not here! Look! Here is the place where they laid him.

verses.name: Mark 16:7
verses.text: But go, and say to his disciples and to Peter ‘He is going before you into Galilee; there you will see him, as he told you.’”

verses.name: Mark 16:8
verses.text: They went out, and fled from the tomb, for they were trembling and bewildered; and they did not say a word to anyone, for they were frightened;  <div eID="gen7256" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Mark 16:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv465"/><div sID="gen7257" type="majorSection"/> <title>A late appendix</title> <div eID="gen7257" type="majorSection"/> <div sID="gen7258" type="majorSection"/> <title>(Inserted in some manuscripts from an ancient source)</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv465"/> after his rising again, early on the first day of the week, Jesus appeared first of all to Mary of Magdala, from whom he had driven out seven demons.

verses.name: Mark 16:10
verses.text: She went and told the news to those who had been with him and who were now in sorrow and tears;

verses.name: Mark 16:11
verses.text: yet even they, when they heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, did not believe it.

verses.name: Mark 16:12
verses.text: Afterwards, altered in appearance, he made himself known to two of them, as they were walking, on their way into the country.

verses.name: Mark 16:13
verses.text: They also went and told the rest, but they did not believe even them.

verses.name: Mark 16:14
verses.text: Later on, he made himself known to the Eleven themselves as they were at a meal, and reproached them with their want of faith and their stubbornness, because they did not believe those who had seen him after he had risen from the dead.

verses.name: Mark 16:15
verses.text: Then he said to them: <q marker="" who="Jesus">“Go into all the world, and proclaim the good news to all creation.</q>

verses.name: Mark 16:16
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who refuses to believe will be condemned.</q>

verses.name: Mark 16:17
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">Moreover these signs will attend those who believe. In my name they will drive out demons; they will speak with ‘tongues’;</q>

verses.name: Mark 16:18
verses.text: <q marker="" who="Jesus">they will take up snakes in their hands; and, if they drink any poison, it will not hurt them; they will place their hands on sick people and they will recover.”</q>

verses.name: Mark 16:19
verses.text: So the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven, and sat at the right hand of God.

verses.name: Mark 16:20
verses.text: But they set out, and made the proclamation everywhere, the Lord working with them, and confirming the message by the signs which attended it.  <div eID="gen7258" type="majorSection"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv466"/><div sID="gen7259" type="majorSection"/> <title>Another appendix But all that had been revealed to them they reported briefly to Peter and his companions. Afterwards Jesus himself sent them out, from east to west, the sacred and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation.</title> <div eID="gen7259" type="majorSection"/> <chapter eID="Mark.16"/> <div eID="gen7063" osisID="Mark" type="book"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:1
verses.text: To his Excellency, Theophilus. <div sID="gen7262" type="paragraph"/> Many attempts have been already made to draw up an because of those events which have reached their conclusion among us,

verses.name: Luke 1:2
verses.text: just as they were reported to us by those who from the beginning were eye-witnesses, and afterwards became bearers of the message.

verses.name: Luke 1:3
verses.text: And, therefore, I also, since I have investigated all these events with great care from their very beginning, have resolved to write a connected history of them for you,

verses.name: Luke 1:4
verses.text: in order that you may be able to satisfy yourself of the accuracy of the story which you have heard from the lips of others.  <div eID="gen7262" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7261" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv466"/><div sID="gen7263" type="majorSection"/> <title>Birth, Parentage, Infancy and Boyhood</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv466"/> In the reign of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the division called after Abijah. His wife, whose name was Elizabeth, was also a descendant of Aaron.

verses.name: Luke 1:6
verses.text: They were both righteous people, who lived blameless lives, guiding their steps by all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.

verses.name: Luke 1:7
verses.text: But they had no child, Elizabeth being barren; and both of them were advanced in years.

verses.name: Luke 1:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv467"/><div sID="gen7264" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv467"/> One day, when Zechariah was officiating as priest before God, during the turn of his division,

verses.name: Luke 1:9
verses.text: it fell to him by lot, in accordance with the practice among the priests, to go into the Temple of the Lord and burn incense;

verses.name: Luke 1:10
verses.text: and, as it was the Hour of Incense, the people were all praying outside.

verses.name: Luke 1:11
verses.text: And an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing on the right of the Altar of Incense.

verses.name: Luke 1:12
verses.text: Zechariah was startled at the sight and was awe-struck.

verses.name: Luke 1:13
verses.text: But the angel said to him: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah; your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, whom you will call by the name John.

verses.name: Luke 1:14
verses.text: He will be to you a joy and a delight; and many will rejoice over his birth.

verses.name: Luke 1:15
verses.text: For he will be great in the sight of the Lord; he will not drink any wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit from the very hour of his birth,

verses.name: Luke 1:16
verses.text: and will reconcile many of the Israelites to the Lord their God.

verses.name: Luke 1:17
verses.text: He will go before him in the spirit and with the power of Elijah, ‘to reconcile fathers to their children’ and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, and so make ready for the Lord a people prepared for him.”  <div eID="gen7264" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv468"/><div sID="gen7265" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv468"/> “How can I be sure of this?” Zechariah asked the angel. “For I am an old man and my wife is advanced in years.”  <div eID="gen7265" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv469"/><div sID="gen7266" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv469"/> “I am Gabriel,” the angel answered, “who stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

verses.name: Luke 1:20
verses.text: And now you will be silent and unable to speak until the day when this takes place, because you did not believe what I said, though my words will be fulfilled in due course.”  <div eID="gen7266" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:21
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv470"/><div sID="gen7267" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv470"/> Meanwhile the people were watching for Zechariah, wondering at his remaining so long in the Temple.

verses.name: Luke 1:22
verses.text: When he came out, he was unable to speak to them, and they perceived that he had seen a vision there. But Zechariah kept making signs to them, and remained dumb.

verses.name: Luke 1:23
verses.text: And, as soon as his term of service was finished, he returned home.

verses.name: Luke 1:24
verses.text: After this his wife, Elizabeth, became pregnant and lived in seclusion for five months.

verses.name: Luke 1:25
verses.text: “The Lord has done this for me,” she said, “he has shown me kindness and taken away the public disgrace of childlessness under which I have been living.”  <div eID="gen7267" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv471"/><div sID="gen7268" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv471"/> Six months later the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a town in Galilee called Nazareth,

verses.name: Luke 1:27
verses.text: to a maiden there who was engaged to a man named Joseph, a descendant of David. Her name was Mary.

verses.name: Luke 1:28
verses.text: Gabriel came into her presence and greeted her, saying: “You have been shown great favor - the Lord is with you..”

verses.name: Luke 1:29
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv472"/><div sID="gen7269" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv472"/> Mary was much disturbed at his words, and was wondering to herself what such a greeting could mean,

verses.name: Luke 1:30
verses.text: when the angel spoke again: “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.

verses.name: Luke 1:31
verses.text: And now, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you will give him the name Jesus.

verses.name: Luke 1:32
verses.text: The child will be great and will be called ‘Son of the Most High,’ and the Lord God will give him the throne of his ancestor David,

verses.name: Luke 1:33
verses.text: and he will reign over the descendants of Jacob for ever; And to his kingdom there will be no end.”  <div eID="gen7269" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:34
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv473"/><div sID="gen7270" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv473"/> “How can this be?” Mary asked the angel. “For I have no husband.”  <div eID="gen7270" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:35
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv474"/><div sID="gen7271" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv474"/> “The Holy Spirit will descend on you,” answered the angel, “and the Power of the Most High will overshadow you; and therefore the child will be called ‘holy,’ and ‘Son of God.’

verses.name: Luke 1:36
verses.text: And Elizabeth, your cousin, is herself also expecting a son in her old age; and it is now the sixth month with her, though she is called barren;

verses.name: Luke 1:37
verses.text: for no promise from God will fail to be fulfilled.”  <div eID="gen7271" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:38
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv475"/><div sID="gen7272" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv475"/> “I am the servant of the Lord,” exclaimed Mary; “let it be with me as you have said.” Then the angel left her.  <div eID="gen7272" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:39
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv476"/><div sID="gen7273" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv476"/> Soon after this Mary set out, and made her way quickly into the hill-country, to a town in Judah;

verses.name: Luke 1:40
verses.text: and there she went into Zechariah’s house and greeted Elizabeth.

verses.name: Luke 1:41
verses.text: When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the child moved within her, and Elizabeth herself was filled with the Holy Spirit,

verses.name: Luke 1:42
verses.text: and cried aloud: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is your unborn child!

verses.name: Luke 1:43
verses.text: But how have I this honor, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?

verses.name: Luke 1:44
verses.text: For, as soon as your greeting reached my ears, the child moved within me with delight!

verses.name: Luke 1:45
verses.text: Happy indeed is she who believed that the promise which she received from the Lord would be fulfilled.”  <div eID="gen7273" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:46
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv477"/><div sID="gen7274" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv477"/> And Mary said: <lg sID="gen7275"/> <l sID="gen7276"/>“My soul exalts the Lord,<l eID="gen7276"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7277"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:47
verses.text: my spirit delights in God my Savior;<l eID="gen7277" level="2"/> <l sID="gen7278"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:48
verses.text: for he has remembered his humble servant girl;<l eID="gen7278"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7279"/>And from this hour all ages will count me happy!<l eID="gen7279" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7275"/> <lg sID="gen7280"/> <l sID="gen7281"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:49
verses.text: Great things has the Almighty done for me;<l eID="gen7281"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7282"/>And holy is his name.<l eID="gen7282" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7283"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:50
verses.text: From age to age his mercy rests<l eID="gen7283" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7284"/>On those who honor him.<l eID="gen7284" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7280"/> <lg sID="gen7285"/> <l sID="gen7286"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:51
verses.text: Mighty are the deeds of his arm;<l eID="gen7286"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7287"/>He scatters the proud with their own devices,<l eID="gen7287" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7288"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:52
verses.text: he casts down princes from their thrones,<l eID="gen7288" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7289"/>and the humble he uplifts,<l eID="gen7289" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7290"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:53
verses.text: the hungry he loads with gifts,<l eID="gen7290" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7291"/>and the rich he sends empty away.<l eID="gen7291" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7285"/> <lg sID="gen7292"/> <l sID="gen7293"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:54
verses.text: He has stretched out his hand to his servant Israel,<l eID="gen7293"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7294"/>Ever mindful of his mercy<l eID="gen7294" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7295"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:55
verses.text: (As he promised to our forefathers)<l eID="gen7295" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7296"/>For Abraham and his race for ever.”<l eID="gen7296" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7292"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:56
verses.text: Mary stayed with Elizabeth about three months, and then returned to her home.

verses.name: Luke 1:57
verses.text: When Elizabeth’s time came, she gave birth to a son;

verses.name: Luke 1:58
verses.text: and her neighbors and relations, hearing of the great goodness of the Lord to her, came to share her joy.

verses.name: Luke 1:59
verses.text: A week later they met to circumcise the child, and were about to call him ‘Zechariah’ after his father,

verses.name: Luke 1:60
verses.text: when his mother spoke up: “No, he is to be called John.”  <div eID="gen7274" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:61
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv478"/><div sID="gen7297" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv478"/> “You have no relation of that name!” they exclaimed;

verses.name: Luke 1:62
verses.text: and they made signs to the child’s father, to find out what he wished the child to be called.

verses.name: Luke 1:63
verses.text: Asking for a writing-tablet, he wrote the words — ‘His name is John.’ Everyone was surprised;

verses.name: Luke 1:64
verses.text: and immediately Zechariah recovered his voice and the use of his tongue, and began to bless God.

verses.name: Luke 1:65
verses.text: All their neighbors were awe-struck at this; and throughout the hill-country of Judea the whole story was much talked about;

verses.name: Luke 1:66
verses.text: and all who heard it kept it in mind, asking one another — “What can this child be destined to become?” For the Power of the Lord was with him.  <div eID="gen7297" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:67
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv479"/><div sID="gen7298" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv479"/> Then his father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit, and, speaking under inspiration, said: <lg sID="gen7299"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7300"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:68
verses.text: “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel,<l eID="gen7300" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7301"/>Who has visited his people and wrought their deliverance,<l eID="gen7301" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7302"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:69
verses.text: and has raised up for us the Strength of our salvation<l eID="gen7302" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7303"/>In the house of his servant David —<l eID="gen7303" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7299"/> <lg sID="gen7304"/> <l sID="gen7305"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:70
verses.text: As he promised by the lips of his holy prophets of old —<l eID="gen7305"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7306"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:71
verses.text: salvation from our enemies and from the hands of all who hate us,<l eID="gen7306" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7307"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:72
verses.text: showing mercy to our forefathers,<l eID="gen7307" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7308"/>And mindful of his sacred covenant.<l eID="gen7308" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7304"/> <lg sID="gen7309"/> <l sID="gen7310"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:73
verses.text: This was the oath which he swore to our forefather Abraham —<l eID="gen7310"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7311"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:74
verses.text: That we should be rescued from the hands of our enemies,<l eID="gen7311" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7312"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:75
verses.text: and should serve him without fear in holiness and righteousness,<l eID="gen7312" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7313"/>In his presence all our days.<l eID="gen7313" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7309"/> <lg sID="gen7314"/> <l sID="gen7315"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:76
verses.text: And you, child, will be called prophet of the Most High,<l eID="gen7315"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7316"/>For you will go before the Lord to make ready his way,<l eID="gen7316" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7317"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:77
verses.text: to give his people the knowledge of salvation<l eID="gen7317" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7318"/>In the forgiveness of their sins,<l eID="gen7318" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7314"/> <lg sID="gen7319"/> <l sID="gen7320"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:78
verses.text: through the tender mercy of our God,<l eID="gen7320"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7321"/>Whereby the Dawn will break on us from heaven,<l eID="gen7321" level="2"/> <l level="1" sID="gen7322"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:79
verses.text: to give light to those who live in darkness and the shadow of death,<l eID="gen7322" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7323"/>And guide our feet into the way of peace.”<l eID="gen7323" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7319"/>

verses.name: Luke 1:80
verses.text: The child grew and became strong in spirit; and he lived in the Wilds until the time came for his appearance before Israel.  <div eID="gen7298" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv480"/><div sID="gen7324" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen7324" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Luke.1"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:1
verses.text: About that time an edict was issued by the Emperor Augustus that a census should be taken of the whole Empire.

verses.name: Luke 2:2
verses.text: (This was the first census taken while Quirinius was Governor of Syria).

verses.name: Luke 2:3
verses.text: And everyone went to his own town to be registered.

verses.name: Luke 2:4
verses.text: Among others Joseph went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Bethlehem, the town of David, in Judea — because he belonged to the family and house of David —

verses.name: Luke 2:5
verses.text: To be registered with Mary, his engaged wife, who was about to become a mother.

verses.name: Luke 2:6
verses.text: While they were there her time came,

verses.name: Luke 2:7
verses.text: and she gave birth to her first child, a son. And because there was no room for them in the inn, she swathed him around and laid him in a manger.

verses.name: Luke 2:8
verses.text: In that same country-side were shepherds out in the open fields, watching their flocks that night,

verses.name: Luke 2:9
verses.text: when an angel of the Lord suddenly stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them; and they were seized with fear.

verses.name: Luke 2:10
verses.text: “Have no fear,” the angel said. “For I bring you good news of a great joy in store for all the nation.

verses.name: Luke 2:11
verses.text: This day there has been born to you, in the town of David, a Savior, who is Christ and Lord.

verses.name: Luke 2:12
verses.text: And this will be the sign for you. You will find the infant swathed, and lying in a manger.”

verses.name: Luke 2:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv480"/><div sID="gen7325" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv480"/> Then suddenly there appeared with the angel a multitude of the heavenly Host, praising God, and singing — <lg sID="gen7326"/> <l sID="gen7327"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:14
verses.text: “glory to God on high,<l eID="gen7327"/> <l level="2" sID="gen7328"/>And on earth peace among those in whom he finds pleasure.”<l eID="gen7328" level="2"/> <lg eID="gen7326"/>

verses.name: Luke 2:15
verses.text: Now, when the angels had left them and gone back to heaven, the shepherds said to one another: “Let us go at once to Bethlehem, and see this thing that has happened, of which the Lord has told us.”

verses.name: Luke 2:16
verses.text: So they went quickly, and found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in a manger;

verses.name: Luke 2:17
verses.text: and, when they saw it, they told of all that had been said to them about this child.

verses.name: Luke 2:18
verses.text: All who heard the shepherds were astonished at their story,

verses.name: Luke 2:19
