verses.text: Slaves, always obey your earthly masters, not only when their eyes are on you, as if you had but to please people alone, but giving them ungrudging service, in your respect for the Master.

verses.name: Colossians 3:23
verses.text: Whatever you do, do it with all your heart, as if working for the Master and not for people,

verses.name: Colossians 3:24
verses.text: since you know that it is from the Master that you will receive the inheritance which will be your reward. You are serving Christ, the Master.

verses.name: Colossians 3:25
verses.text: Those who do wrong will reap the wrong they have done; and there will be no partiality.  <chapter eID="Col.3"/>

verses.name: Colossians 4:1
verses.text: Masters, do what is right and fair by your slaves, for you know that you also have a Master — in heaven.  <div eID="gen8542" type="section"/>

verses.name: Colossians 4:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1202"/><div sID="gen8543" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1202"/> Devote yourselves to prayer. Give your whole mind to it, and also offer thanksgiving;

verses.name: Colossians 4:3
verses.text: and at the same time pray for us, so that God may give us an opening for our message, so that we may speak of the truths hidden in the Christ — the truths for which I am in chains!

verses.name: Colossians 4:4
verses.text: Then I will make them known, as I ought to do.

verses.name: Colossians 4:5
verses.text: Show tact in your behavior to the outside world, making the most of every opportunity.

verses.name: Colossians 4:6
verses.text: Let your conversation always be kindly, but not bland, season it, as it were, with salt; be aware in each case of the answer you should be giving.  <div eID="gen8543" type="section"/> <div eID="gen8540" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Colossians 4:7
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1203"/><div sID="gen8544" type="majorSection"/> <title>Conclusion</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1203"/> Our dear friend, Tychicus, will tell you all about me. He is a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Master’s cause.

verses.name: Colossians 4:8
verses.text: I send him to you expressly that you may learn our circumstances, and that he may give you encouragement.

verses.name: Colossians 4:9
verses.text: With him will be Onesimus, our dear faithful friend, who is one of yourselves. They will tell you all that is going on here.

verses.name: Colossians 4:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1204"/><div sID="gen8545" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1204"/> My fellow prisoner, Aristarchus, sends you his greeting, and Barnabas’s cousin, Mark, sends his. (You have received directions about him. If he comes to you, make him welcome.)

verses.name: Colossians 4:11
verses.text: Joshua, who is called Justus, also sends his greeting. These are the only converts from Judaism who have worked with me for the kingdom of God; I have found them a great comfort.

verses.name: Colossians 4:12
verses.text: Epaphras, who is one of yourselves, sends you his greeting. He is a servant of Christ Jesus, and is always most earnest in your behalf in his prayers, praying that you may stand firm, with a matured faith and with a sure conviction of all that is in accordance with God’s will.

verses.name: Colossians 4:13
verses.text: I can bear testimony to the deep interest he takes in you, as well as in the followers at Laodicea and at Hierapolis.

verses.name: Colossians 4:14
verses.text: Luke, our dear doctor, sends you his greeting, and Demas sends his.

verses.name: Colossians 4:15
verses.text: Give my greeting to the followers at Laodicea, and to Nymphe, and to the church that meets at her house.

verses.name: Colossians 4:16
verses.text: And when this letter has been read to you, see that it is also read before the church at Laodicea, and that you yourselves read the letter which will be forwarded from there.

verses.name: Colossians 4:17
verses.text: Give this message to Archippus — ‘Take care to discharge to the best of your ability the office to which you were appointed in the Master’s cause.’  <div eID="gen8545" type="section"/>

verses.name: Colossians 4:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1205"/><div sID="gen8546" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1205"/> I, Paul, add this greeting in my own handwriting. Remember these chains of mine. God’s blessing be with you.  <div eID="gen8546" type="section"/> <div eID="gen8544" type="majorSection"/> <chapter eID="Col.4"/> <div eID="gen8530" osisID="Col" type="book"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:1
verses.text: To the Thessalonian church in union with God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, from Paul, Silas, and Timothy. May God bless you and give you peace.  <div eID="gen8548" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:2
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1206"/><div sID="gen8549" type="majorSection"/> <title>The Apostle and his Converts</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1206"/> We always mention you in our prayers and thank God for you all;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:3
verses.text: recalling continually before our God and Father the efforts that have resulted from your faith, the toil prompted by your love, and the patient endurance sustained by your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:4
verses.text: Friends, whom God loves, we know that he has chosen you,

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:5
verses.text: because the good news that we brought came home to you, not merely as so many words, but with a power and a fulness of conviction due to the Holy Spirit. For you know the life that we lived among you for your good.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:6
verses.text: And you yourselves began to follow, not only our example, but the Master’s also; and, in spite of much suffering, you welcomed the message with a joy inspired by the Holy Spirit,

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:7
verses.text: and so became a pattern to all who believed in Christ throughout Macedonia and Greece.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:8
verses.text: For it was from you that the Lord’s message resounded throughout Macedonia and Greece; and, more than that, your faith in God has become known far and wide; so that there is no need for us to say another word.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:9
verses.text: Indeed, in speaking about us, the people themselves tell of the reception you gave us, and how, turning to God from your idols, you became servants of the true and living God,

verses.name: I Thessalonians 1:10
verses.text: and are now awaiting the return from heaven of his Son whom he raised from the dead — Jesus, our deliverer from the coming wrath.  <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1207"/><div sID="gen8550" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8550" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="1Thess.1"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:1
verses.text: Yes, friends, you yourselves know that your reception of us was not without result.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:2
verses.text: For, although we had experienced suffering and ill treatment, as you know, at Philippi, we had the courage, by the help of our God, to tell you God’s good news in spite of great opposition.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:3
verses.text: Our appeal to you was not based on a delusion, nor was it made from unworthy motives, or with any intention of misleading you.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:4
verses.text: But, having been found worthy by God to be entrusted with the good news, therefore we tell it; with a view to please, not people, but God who proves our hearts.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:5
verses.text: Never at any time, as you know, did we use the language of flattery, or make false professions in order to hide selfish aims. God will bear witness to that.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:6
verses.text: Nor did we seek to win honor from people, whether from you or from others, although, as apostles of Christ, we might have burdened you with our support.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:7
verses.text: But we lived among you with the simplicity of a child; we were like a woman nursing her own children.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:8
verses.text: In our strong affection for you, that seemed to us the best way of sharing with you, not only God’s Good news, but our lives as well — so dear had you become to us.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:9
verses.text: You will not have forgotten, friends, our labor and toil. Night and day we used to work at our trades, so as not be a burden to any of you, while we proclaimed to you God’s good news.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:10
verses.text: You will bear witness, and God also, that our relations with you who believed in Christ were pure, and upright, and beyond reproach.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:11
verses.text: Indeed, you know that, like a father with his own children, we used to encourage and comfort every one of you, and solemnly plead with you;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:12
verses.text: so that you should make your daily lives worthy of God who is calling you into the glory of his kingdom.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1207"/><div sID="gen8551" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1207"/> This, too, is a reason why we, on our part, are continually thanking God — because, in receiving the teaching that you had from us, you accepted it, not as the teaching of humans, but as what it really is — the teaching of God, which is even now doing its work within you who believe in Christ.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:14
verses.text: For you, friends, began to follow the example of the churches of God in Judea which are in union with Jesus Christ; you, in your turn, suffering at the hands of your fellow citizens, in the same way as those churches did at the hands of of their people —

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:15
verses.text: who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and persecuted us also. They do not try to please God, and they are enemies to all humanity,

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:16
verses.text: for they try to prevent us from speaking to the Gentiles with a view to their salvation, and so are always ‘filling up the measure of their iniquity.’ But the wrath of God has come upon them to the full!

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1208"/><div sID="gen8552" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1208"/> As for ourselves, friends, our having been bereaved of you even for a short time — though in body only, and not in spirit — made us all the more eager to see your faces again; and the longing to do so was strong on us.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:18
verses.text: That was why we made up our minds to go and see you — at least I, Paul, did, more than once — but Satan put difficulties in our way.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:19
verses.text: For what hope or joy will be ours, or what crown will we have to boast of, in the presence of our Lord Jesus, at his coming, if it be not you?

verses.name: I Thessalonians 2:20
verses.text: You are our pride and our delight!  <div eID="gen8552" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1209"/><div sID="gen8553" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8553" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="1Thess.2"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:1
verses.text: And so, as we could bear it no longer, we made up our minds to remain behind alone at Athens,

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:2
verses.text: and sent Timothy, our dear friend and God’s minister of the good news of the Christ, to strengthen you, and to encourage you in your faith,

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:3
verses.text: so that none of you should be shaken by the troubles through which you are passing. You yourselves know that we are destined to meet with such things.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:4
verses.text: For, even while we were with you, we warned you beforehand that we were certain to encounter trouble. And so it proved, as you know.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:5
verses.text: Therefore, since I could no longer endure the uncertainty, I sent to make inquiries about your faith, fearing that the Tempter had tempted you, and that our toil might prove to have been in vain.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:6
verses.text: But, when Timothy recently returned to us from you with good news of your faith and love, and told us how kindly you think of us — always longing, he said, to see us, just as we are longing to see you —

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:7
verses.text: on hearing this, we felt encouraged about you, friends, in the midst of all our difficulties and troubles, by your faith.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:8
verses.text: For it is new life to us to know that you are holding fast to the Lord.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:9
verses.text: How can we thank God enough for all the happiness that you are giving us in the sight of our God?

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:10
verses.text: Night and day we pray most earnestly that we may see you face to face, and make good any deficiency in your faith.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1209"/><div sID="gen8554" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1209"/> May our God and Father himself, and Jesus, our Lord, make the way plain for us to come to you.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:12
verses.text: And for you, may the Lord fill you to overflowing with love for one another and for everyone, just as we are filled with love for you;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 3:13
verses.text: and so make your hearts strong, and your lives pure beyond reproach, in the sight of our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus, with all his Holy Ones.  <div eID="gen8554" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8551" type="section"/> <chapter eID="1Thess.3"/> <div eID="gen8549" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:1
verses.text: Further, friends, we beg and urge you in the name of our Lord Jesus to carry out more fully than ever — as indeed you are already doing — all that you have heard from us as to what your daily life must be, if it is to please God.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:2
verses.text: For you have not forgotten the directions that we gave you on the authority of our Lord Jesus.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1210"/><div sID="gen8556" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1210"/> For this is God’s purpose — that you should be pure; abstaining from all immorality;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:4
verses.text: each of you learning to gain control over your own body, in a way that is holy and honorable,

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:5
verses.text: and not for the mere gratification of your passions, like the Gentiles who know nothing of God;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:6
verses.text: none of you overreaching or taking advantage of their fellow follower of the Lord in such matters. ‘The Lord takes vengeance’ on all who do such things, as we have already warned you and solemnly declared.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:7
verses.text: For God’s call to us does not permit of an impure life, but demands purity.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:8
verses.text: Therefore the person who disregards this warning disregards, not people, but God who gives you his Holy Spirit.  <div eID="gen8556" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1211"/><div sID="gen8557" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1211"/> As to love for each other there is no need to write to you; for you have yourselves been taught by God to love one another;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:10
verses.text: and indeed you do act in this spirit towards all his people throughout Macedonia. <div eID="gen8557" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen8558" type="paragraph"/> Yet, friends, we beg you to do even more.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:11
verses.text: Make it your ambition to live quietly, and to attend to your own business, and to work with your hands, as we directed you;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:12
verses.text: so that your conduct may win respect from those outside the church, and that you may not want for anything.  <div eID="gen8558" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8555" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1212"/><div sID="gen8559" type="majorSection"/> <title>The Dead in Christ at the coming of the Lord</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1212"/> We don't want you to be ignorant, friends, about those who have passed to their rest. We don't want you to grieve like other people who have no hope.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:14
verses.text: For, as we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also we believe that God will bring, with Jesus, those who through him have passed to their rest.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:15
verses.text: This we tell you on the authority of the Lord — that those of us who are still living at the coming of the Lord will not anticipate those who have passed to their rest.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:16
verses.text: For, with a loud summons, with the shout of an archangel, and with the trumpet-call of God, the Lord himself will come down from heaven.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:17
verses.text: Then those who died in union with Christ will rise first; and afterwards we who are still living will be caught up in the clouds, with them, to meet the Lord in the air; and so we will be for ever with the Lord.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 4:18
verses.text: Therefore, comfort one another with what I have told you.  <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1213"/><div sID="gen8560" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8560" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="1Thess.4"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:1
verses.text: But as to the times and the moments, there is no need, friends, for anyone to write to you.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:2
verses.text: You yourselves know well that the day of the Lord will come just as a thief comes in the night.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:3
verses.text: When people are saying ‘All is quiet and safe,’ it is then that, like birth pains on a pregnant woman, ruin comes suddenly upon them, and there will be no escape!

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:4
verses.text: You, however, friends, are not in darkness, that the daylight should take you by surprise as if you were thieves.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:5
verses.text: For you all are ‘sons of light’ and ‘sons of the day.’ <div sID="gen8561" type="paragraph"/> We have nothing to do with night, or darkness.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:6
verses.text: Therefore let us not sleep as others do. No, let us be watchful and self-controlled.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:7
verses.text: It is at night that people sleep, and at night that drunkards get drunk.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:8
verses.text: But let us, who belong to the day, control ourselves, and put on faith and love as a breast plate, and the hope of salvation as a helmet.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:9
verses.text: For God destined us, not for wrath, but to win salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, who died for us,

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:10
verses.text: that, whether we are still watching or have fallen asleep, we may live with him.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:11
verses.text: Therefore encourage one another, and try to build up one another’s characters, as indeed you are doing.  <div eID="gen8561" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8559" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1213"/><div sID="gen8562" type="majorSection"/> <title>Conclusion</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1213"/> We beg you, friends, to value those who toil among you, and are your leaders in the Lord’s service, and give you counsel.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:13
verses.text: Hold them in the very greatest esteem and affection for the sake of their work. Live at peace with one another.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:14
verses.text: We entreat you also, friends — warn the disorderly, comfort the faint-hearted, give a helping hand to the weak, and be patient with everyone.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:15
verses.text: Take care that none of you ever pays back wrong for wrong, but always follow the kindest course with one another and with everyone.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:16
verses.text: Always be joyful;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:17
verses.text: never cease to pray;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:18
verses.text: under all circumstances give thanks to God. For this is his will for you as made known in Christ Jesus.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:19
verses.text: Do not quench the Spirit;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:20
verses.text: do not make light of preaching.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:21
verses.text: Bring everything to the test; cling to what is good;

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:22
verses.text: shun every form of evil.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:23
verses.text: May God himself, the giver of peace, make you altogether holy; and may your spirits, souls, and bodies be kept altogether faultless until the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:24
verses.text: He who calls you will not fail you; he will complete his work.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:25
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1214"/><div sID="gen8563" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1214"/> Friends, pray for us.  <div eID="gen8563" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:26
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1215"/><div sID="gen8564" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1215"/> Greet all the Lord's followers with a sacred kiss.

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:27
verses.text: I order you in the Lord’s name to have this letter read to all the brethren.  <div eID="gen8564" type="section"/>

verses.name: I Thessalonians 5:28
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1216"/><div sID="gen8565" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1216"/> May the blessing of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.  <div eID="gen8565" type="section"/> <div eID="gen8562" type="majorSection"/> <chapter eID="1Thess.5"/> <div eID="gen8547" osisID="1Thess" type="book"/>

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:1
verses.text: To the Thessalonian church in union with God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, From Paul, Silas, and Timothy.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:2
verses.text: May God, the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ bless you and give you peace.  <div eID="gen8567" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1217"/><div sID="gen8568" type="majorSection"/> <title>The Apostle and his Converts</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1217"/> Friends, it is our duty always to thank God about you, as is but right, considering the wonderful growth of your faith, and because, without exception, your love for one another is continually increasing.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:4
verses.text: So much is this the case that we ourselves speak with pride, before the churches of God, of the patience and faith which you have shown, in spite of all the persecutions and troubles that you are enduring.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:5
verses.text: These persecutions will vindicate the justice of God’s judgment, and will result in your being reckoned worthy of God’s kingdom, for the sake of which you are now suffering;

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:6
verses.text: since God deems it just to inflict suffering on those who are now inflicting suffering on you,

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:7
verses.text: and to give relief to you who are suffering, as well as to us, at the appearing of the Lord Jesus from heaven with his mighty angels, ‘in flaming fire.’

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:8
verses.text: Then he will ‘inflict punishment on those who refuse to know God, and on those who turn a deaf ear’ to the good news of Jesus, our Lord.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:9
verses.text: They will pay the penalty of unutterable ruin — banished ‘from the presence of the Lord and from the glorious manifestation of his might,

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:10
verses.text: when he comes to be honor ed in his people,’ and to be revered in all who have learned to believe in him (for you also believed our testimony) — as he will be on ‘that day.’

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:11
verses.text: With this in view, our constant prayer for you is that our God may count you worthy of the call that you have received, and by his power make perfect your delight in all goodness and the efforts that have resulted from your faith.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 1:12
verses.text: Then, in the loving kindness of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ, will the name of Jesus, our Lord, be honored in you, and you in him.  <chapter eID="2Thess.1"/> <div eID="gen8568" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:1
verses.text: As to the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and our being gathered to meet him, we beg you, friends,

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:2
verses.text: not lightly to let your minds become unsettled, or disturbed by any revelation, or by any message, or by any letter, purporting to come from us, to the effect that the day of the Lord is come.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:3
verses.text: Do not let anyone deceive you, whatever he may do. For it will not come until after the Great Apostasy, and the appearing of that Incarnation of Wickedness, that the Lost soul,

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:4
verses.text: who so opposes himself to everyone that is spoken of as a God or as an object of worship, and so exalts himself above them, that he seats himself in the Temple of God, and displays himself as God!

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:5
verses.text: Do not you remember how, when I was with you, I used to speak to you of all this?

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:6
verses.text: And you know now what the restraining influence is which prevents his appearing before his appointed time.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:7
verses.text: Wickedness, indeed, is already at work in secret; but only until he who at present restrains it is removed out of the way.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:8
verses.text: Then will ‘Wickedness Incarnate’ appear, but the Lord Jesus will destroy him with the breath of his lips, and annihilate him by the splendor of his coming.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:9
verses.text: For at the coming of the Lord there will be great activity on the part of Satan, in the form of all kinds of deceptive miracles, signs, and marvels, as well as of wicked attempts to delude —

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:10
verses.text: to the ruin of those who are on the path to destruction, because they have never received and loved the truth to their own salvation.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:11
verses.text: That is why God places them under the influence of a delusion, to cause them to believe a lie;

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:12
verses.text: so that sentence may be passed on all those who refuse to believe the truth, but delight in wickedness.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:13
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1218"/><div sID="gen8570" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1218"/> But, friends, whom the Lord loves, it is our duty always to thank God about you, for, from the first, God chose you for salvation through the purifying influence of the Spirit, and your belief in the truth.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:14
verses.text: To this you were called by the good news which we brought you, to attain to the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:15
verses.text: Stand firm then, friends, and hold fast to the truths that we taught you, whether by word or by letter.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:16
verses.text: And may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and, in his loving kindness, gave us unfailing consolation and good ground for hope,

verses.name: II Thessalonians 2:17
verses.text: console your hearts, and strengthen you to do and to say all that is right.  <div eID="gen8570" type="section"/> <chapter eID="2Thess.2"/> <div eID="gen8569" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:1
verses.text: In conclusion, friends, pray for us — pray that the Lord’s message may spread rapidly, and be received everywhere with honor, as it was among you;

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:2
verses.text: and that we may be preserved from wrong-headed and wicked people — for it is not everyone who believes in Christ.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:3
verses.text: But the Lord will not fail you; he will give you strength, and guard you from evil.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:4
verses.text: Yes, and the confidence that our union with the Lord enables us to place in you leads us to believe that you are doing, and will do, what we direct you.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:5
verses.text: May the Lord bring you to the love of God, and to the patience of the Christ.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1219"/><div sID="gen8572" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1219"/> We beg you, friends, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, to avoid any follower who is living an ill-ordered life, which is not in agreement with the teaching that you received from us.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:7
verses.text: For you know well that you ought to follow our example. When we were with you, our life was not ill-ordered,

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:8
verses.text: nor did we eat anyone’s bread without paying for it. Night and day, laboring and toiling, we used to work at our trades, so as not to be a burden on any of you.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:9
verses.text: This was not because we had not a right to receive support, but our object was to give you a pattern for you to copy.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:10
verses.text: Indeed, when we were with you, the rule we laid down was — ‘Whoever does not choose to work will not get to eat.’

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:11
verses.text: We hear that there are among you people who are living ill-ordered lives, and who, instead of attending to their own business, are mere busybodies.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:12
verses.text: All such people we beg, and implore,, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, to attend quietly to their business, and earn their own living.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:13
verses.text: You, friends, must not grow weary of doing what is right.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:14
verses.text: If anyone disregards what we have said in this letter, take note of them and avoid their company, so that they may feel ashamed.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:15
verses.text: Yet do not think of them as an enemy, but caution them as you would a brother or sister.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:16
verses.text: May the Lord, from whom all peace comes, himself give you his peace at all times and in all ways. May he be with you all.  <div eID="gen8572" type="section"/>

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1220"/><div sID="gen8573" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1220"/> I, Paul, add this greeting in my own handwriting. It is my signature to every letter. This is how I write.

verses.name: II Thessalonians 3:18
verses.text: May the blessing of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.  <div eID="gen8573" type="section"/> <div eID="gen8571" type="majorSection"/> <chapter eID="2Thess.3"/> <div eID="gen8566" osisID="2Thess" type="book"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 1:1
verses.text: From Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the appointment of God, our Savior, and Christ Jesus, our hope.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:2
verses.text: To Timothy, my true child in the faith: May God, the Father, and Christ Jesus, our Lord, bless you, and be merciful to you, and give you peace.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1221"/><div sID="gen8576" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1221"/> I beg you, as I did when I was on my way into Macedonia, to remain at Ephesus; that you may instruct certain people there not to teach new and strange doctrines,

verses.name: I Timothy 1:4
verses.text: nor to devote their attention to legends and interminable genealogies, which tend to give rise to argument rather than to further that divine plan which is revealed in the faith.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:5
verses.text: The object of all instruction is to call forth that love which comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and a sincere faith.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:6
verses.text: And it is because they have not aimed at these things that the attention of certain people has been diverted to unprofitable subjects.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:7
verses.text: They want to be teachers of the law, and yet do not understand either the words they use, or the subjects on which they speak so confidently.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:8
verses.text: We know, of course, that the law is excellent, when used legitimately,

verses.name: I Timothy 1:9
verses.text: by one who recognizes that laws were not made for good people, but for the lawless and disorderly, for irreligious and wicked people, for those who are irreverent and profane, for those who ill-treat their fathers or mothers, for murderers,

verses.name: I Timothy 1:10
verses.text: for the immoral, for perverts, for slave-dealers, for liars, for perjurers, and for whatever else is opposed to sound Christian teaching —

verses.name: I Timothy 1:11
verses.text: as is taught in the glorious good news of the ever-blessed God, with which I was entrusted.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:12
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1222"/><div sID="gen8577" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1222"/> I am thankful to Christ Jesus, our Lord, who has been my strength, for showing that he thought me worthy of trust by appointing me to his ministry,

verses.name: I Timothy 1:13
verses.text: though I once used to blaspheme, and to persecute, and to insult. Yet mercy was shown me, because I acted in ignorance, while still an unbeliever;

verses.name: I Timothy 1:14
verses.text: and the loving kindness of our Lord was boundless, and filled me with that faith and love which come from union with Christ Jesus.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:15
verses.text: How true the saying is, and worthy of the fullest acceptance, that ‘Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners’! And there is no greater sinner than I!

verses.name: I Timothy 1:16
verses.text: Yet mercy was shown me for the express purpose that Christ Jesus might exhibit in my case, beyond all others, his exhaustless patience, as an example for those who were afterwards to believe on him and attain eternal life.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:17
verses.text: To the eternal King, ever-living, invisible, the one God, be ascribed honor and glory for ever and ever. Amen.  <div eID="gen8577" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 1:18
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1223"/><div sID="gen8578" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1223"/> This, then, is the charge that I lay on you, Timothy, my child, in accordance with what was predicted of you — Fight the good fight in the spirit of those predictions,

verses.name: I Timothy 1:19
verses.text: with faith, and with a clear conscience; and it is because they have thrust this aside, that, as regards the faith, some have wrecked their lives.

verses.name: I Timothy 1:20
verses.text: Hymenaeus and Alexander are instances — the men whom I delivered over to Satan so that they might be taught not to blaspheme.  <div eID="gen8578" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8576" type="section"/> <chapter eID="1Tim.1"/> <div eID="gen8575" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 2:1
verses.text: First of all, then, I ask that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings should be offered for everyone,

verses.name: I Timothy 2:2
verses.text: especially for kings and all who are in high positions, in order that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in a deeply religious and reverent spirit.

verses.name: I Timothy 2:3
verses.text: This will be good and acceptable in the eyes of God, our Savior,

verses.name: I Timothy 2:4
verses.text: whose will is that everyone should be saved, and attain to a full knowledge of the truth.

verses.name: I Timothy 2:5
verses.text: There is but one God, and one mediator between God and men — the man, Christ Jesus,

verses.name: I Timothy 2:6
verses.text: who gave himself as a ransom on behalf of all men. <div sID="gen8580" type="paragraph"/> This must be our testimony, as opportunities present themselves;

verses.name: I Timothy 2:7
verses.text: and it was for this that I was myself appointed a herald and an apostle (I am telling the simple truth and no lie) — a teacher of the Gentiles in the faith and truth.  <div eID="gen8580" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 2:8
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1224"/><div sID="gen8581" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1224"/> My desire, then, is that it should be the custom everywhere for the men to lead the prayers, with hands reverently uplifted, avoiding heated controversy.  <div eID="gen8581" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 2:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1225"/><div sID="gen8582" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1225"/> I also desire that women should adorn themselves with appropriate dress, worn quietly and modestly, and not with wreaths or gold ornaments for the hair, or pearls, or costly clothing,

verses.name: I Timothy 2:10
verses.text: but — as is proper for women who profess to be religious — with good actions.

verses.name: I Timothy 2:11
verses.text: They must learn, listening quietly to their teachers and showing them all deference.

verses.name: I Timothy 2:12
verses.text: I do not consent to them becoming teachers, or exercising authority over men; they ought to not make a fuss.

verses.name: I Timothy 2:13
verses.text: Adam was formed first, not Eve.

verses.name: I Timothy 2:14
verses.text: And it was not Adam who was deceived; it was the woman who was entirely deceived and fell into sin.

verses.name: I Timothy 2:15
verses.text: But she will be saved by the birth of a child, if they never abandon faith, love, or holiness, and behave with modesty.  <div eID="gen8582" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="1Tim.2"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 3:1
verses.text: <div sID="gen8583" type="paragraph"/> How true is this saying: ‘To aspire to be to be a presiding officer in the church is to be ambitious for a noble task.’

verses.name: I Timothy 3:2
verses.text: The presiding officer should be of blameless character; a faithful partner; living a temperate, discreet, and well-ordered life; hospitable, and a skillful teacher,

verses.name: I Timothy 3:3
verses.text: not addicted to drink or brawling, but of a forbearing and peaceable disposition, and not a lover of money;

verses.name: I Timothy 3:4
verses.text: they should provide for own household well, and their children should kept under control and be well-behaved.

verses.name: I Timothy 3:5
verses.text: If someone does not know how to provide for their own household, how can they take charge of the church of God?

verses.name: I Timothy 3:6
verses.text: The presiding officer should not be a recent convert, or they might become blinded by pride and fall under the same condemnation as the devil.

verses.name: I Timothy 3:7
verses.text: They should also be well spoken of by outsiders, so that they may not incur censure and so fall into the devil's trap.

verses.name: I Timothy 3:8
verses.text: So, too, assistant officers should be serious and straightforward, not given to taking much drink or to questionable money-making,

verses.name: I Timothy 3:9
verses.text: but people who hold the deep truths of the faith and have a clear conscience.

verses.name: I Timothy 3:10
verses.text: They should be tested first, and only appointed to their office if no objection is raised against them.

verses.name: I Timothy 3:11
verses.text: It should be the same with the women in this office. They should be serious, not gossips, sober, and trustworthy in all respects.

verses.name: I Timothy 3:12
verses.text: Assistant officers should be faithful partners who manage their children and their households well.

verses.name: I Timothy 3:13
verses.text: Those who have filled that post with honor gain for themselves an honorable position, as well as great confidence through the faith that they place in Christ Jesus.  <div eID="gen8583" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8579" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 3:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1226"/><div sID="gen8584" type="majorSection"/> <title>Special Directions to Timothy</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1226"/> I am writing this to you, though I hope that I will come to see you before long;

verses.name: I Timothy 3:15
verses.text: but in case I should be delayed, I want you to know what your conduct ought to be in the Household of God, which is the church of the living God — the pillar and stay of the truth.

verses.name: I Timothy 3:16
verses.text: Yes, and confessedly wonderful are the deep truths of our religion; for — <lg sID="gen8585"/> <l level="1" sID="gen8586"/>‘He was revealed in our nature,<l eID="gen8586" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen8587"/>Pronounced righteous in spirit,<l eID="gen8587" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen8588"/>Seen by angels,<l eID="gen8588" level="3"/> <l level="1" sID="gen8589"/>Proclaimed among the Gentiles,<l eID="gen8589" level="1"/> <l level="2" sID="gen8590"/>Believed on in the world,<l eID="gen8590" level="2"/> <l level="3" sID="gen8591"/>Taken up into glory.’<l eID="gen8591" level="3"/> <lg eID="gen8585"/>  <chapter eID="1Tim.3"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 4:1
verses.text: But the Spirit distinctly says that in later times there will be some who will fall away from the faith, and devote their attention to misleading spirits, and to the teaching of demons,

verses.name: I Timothy 4:2
verses.text: who will make use of the hypocrisy of lying teachers. These people’s consciences are seared,

verses.name: I Timothy 4:3
verses.text: and they discourage marriage and enjoin abstinence from certain kinds of food; though God created these foods to be enjoyed thankfully by those who hold the faith and have attained a full knowledge of the truth.

verses.name: I Timothy 4:4
verses.text: Everything created by God is good, and there in nothing that need be rejected — provided only that it is received thankfully;

verses.name: I Timothy 4:5
verses.text: for it is consecrated by God’s blessing and by prayer.

verses.name: I Timothy 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1227"/><div sID="gen8592" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1227"/> Put all this before the followers, and you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, sustained by the precepts of the faith and of that good teaching by which you have guided your life.

verses.name: I Timothy 4:7
verses.text: As for profane legends and old wives’ tales, leave them alone. Train yourself to lead a religious life;

verses.name: I Timothy 4:8
verses.text: for while the training of the body is of service in some respects, religion is of service in all, carrying with it, as it does, a promise of life both here and hereafter.

verses.name: I Timothy 4:9
verses.text: How true that saying is and worthy of the fullest acceptance!

verses.name: I Timothy 4:10
verses.text: With that aim we toil and struggle, for we have set our hopes on the living God, who is the Savior of all, and especially of those who hold the faith.  <div eID="gen8592" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 4:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1228"/><div sID="gen8593" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1228"/> Remember these things in your teaching.

verses.name: I Timothy 4:12
verses.text: Do not let anyone look down on you because you are young, but, by your conversation, your conduct, your love, your faith, and your purity, be an example to those who hold the faith.

verses.name: I Timothy 4:13
verses.text: Until I come, apply yourself to public reading, preaching, and teaching.

verses.name: I Timothy 4:14
verses.text: Do not neglect the divine gift within you, which was given you, amid many a prediction, when the hands of the officers of the church were laid on your head.

verses.name: I Timothy 4:15
verses.text: Practice these things, devote yourself to them, so that your progress may be plain to everyone.

verses.name: I Timothy 4:16
verses.text: Look to yourself as well as to your teaching. Persevere in this, for your doing so will mean salvation for yourself as well as for your hearers.  <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1229"/><div sID="gen8594" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8594" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="1Tim.4"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 5:1
verses.text: Do not reprimand an older man, but plead with him as if he were your father. Treat the young men as brothers,

verses.name: I Timothy 5:2
verses.text: the older women as mothers, and the younger women as sisters — with all purity.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:3
verses.text: Show consideration for widows — I mean those who are really widowed.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:4
verses.text: but, if a widow has children or grandchildren, let them learn to show proper regard for the members of their own family first, and to make some return to their parents; for that is pleasing in God’s sight.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:5
verses.text: As for the woman who is really widowed and left quite alone, her hopes are fixed on God, and she devotes herself to prayers and supplications night and day.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:6
verses.text: But the life of a widow who is devoted to pleasure is a living death.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:7
verses.text: Those are the points you should teach, so that there may be no call for your censure.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:8
verses.text: Anyone who fails to provide for their own relations, and especially for those under their own roof, has disowned the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:9
verses.text: A widow, when her name is added to the list, should not be less than sixty years old; she should have been a faithful wife,

verses.name: I Timothy 5:10
verses.text: and be well spoken of for her kind actions. She should have brought up children, have shown hospitality to strangers, have washed the feet of her fellow Christians, have relieved those who were in distress, and devoted herself to every kind of good action.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:11
verses.text: But you should exclude the younger widows from the list; for, when they grow restive under the yoke of the Christ, they want to marry,

verses.name: I Timothy 5:12
verses.text: and so they bring condemnation on themselves for having broken their previous promise.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:13
verses.text: And not only that, but they learn to be idle as they go about from house to house. Nor are they merely idle, but they also become gossips and busybodies, and talk of what they ought not.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:14
verses.text: Therefore I advise young widows to marry, bear children, and attend to their homes, and so avoid giving the enemy an opportunity for scandal.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:15
verses.text: There are some who have already left us, to follow Satan.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:16
verses.text: Any Christian woman, who has relations who are widows, ought to relieve them and not allow them to become a burden to the church, so that the church may relieve those widows who are really widowed.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1229"/><div sID="gen8595" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1229"/> Those officers of the church who fill their office well should be held deserving of especial consideration, particularly those whose work lies in preaching and teaching.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:18
verses.text: The words of scripture are — <lg sID="gen8596"/> <l sID="gen8597"/>‘You should not muzzle the ox while it is treading out the grain.’<l eID="gen8597"/> <lg eID="gen8596"/> and again — <lg sID="gen8598"/> <l sID="gen8599"/><q marker="" who="Jesus">‘The worker is worth their wages.’</q><l eID="gen8599"/> <lg eID="gen8598"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 5:19
verses.text: Do not receive a charge against an officer of the church, unless it is supported by two or three witnesses;

verses.name: I Timothy 5:20
verses.text: but rebuke offenders publicly, so that others may take warning.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:21
verses.text: I charge you solemnly, before God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels, to carry out these directions, unswayed by prejudice, never acting with partiality.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:22
verses.text: Never ordain anyone hastily, and take no part in the wrong-doing of others. Keep your life pure.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:23
verses.text: Do not continue to drink water only, but take a little wine because of the weakness of your stomach, and your frequent ailments.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:24
verses.text: There are some people whose sins are conspicuous and lead on to judgment, while there are others whose sins dog their steps.

verses.name: I Timothy 5:25
verses.text: In the same way noble deeds become conspicuous, and those which are otherwise cannot be concealed.  <div eID="gen8595" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1230"/><div sID="gen8600" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8600" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="1Tim.5"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 6:1
verses.text: All who are in the position of slaves should regard their masters as deserving of the greatest respect, so that the name of God, and our teaching, may not be maligned.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:2
verses.text: Those who have Christian masters should not think less of them because they are also followers of Christ, but on the contrary they should serve them all the better, because those who are to benefit by their good work are dear to them as their fellow Christians.  <div eID="gen8593" type="section"/> <div eID="gen8584" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 6:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1230"/><div sID="gen8601" type="majorSection"/> <title>Conclusion Those are the things to insist on in your teaching.</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1230"/> Anyone who teaches otherwise, and refuses their assent to sound instruction — the instruction of our Lord Jesus Christ — and to the teaching of religion,

verses.name: I Timothy 6:4
verses.text: is puffed up with conceit, not really knowing anything, but having a morbid craving for discussions and arguments. Such things only give rise to envy, quarreling, recriminations, base suspicions,

verses.name: I Timothy 6:5
verses.text: and incessant wrangling on the part of these corrupt-minded people who have lost all hold on the truth, and who think of religion only as a source of gain.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:6
verses.text: And a great source of gain religion is, when it brings contentment with it!

verses.name: I Timothy 6:7
verses.text: For we brought nothing into the world, because we cannot even carry anything out of it.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:8
verses.text: So, with food and shelter, we will be content.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:9
verses.text: Those who want to be rich fall into the net of temptation, and become the prey of many foolish and harmful ambitions, which plunge people into destruction and ruin.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:10
verses.text: Love of money is a source of all kinds of evil; and in their eagerness to be rich some have wandered away from the faith, and have been pierced to the heart by many a regret.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1231"/><div sID="gen8602" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1231"/> But you must, servant of God, avoid all this. Aim at righteousness, piety, faith, love, endurance, gentleness.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:12
verses.text: Run the great race of the faith, and win the eternal life. It was for this that you received the call, and, in the presence of many witnesses, made the great profession of faith.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:13
verses.text: I beg you, as in the sight of God, the source of all life, and of Christ Jesus who before Pontius Pilate made the great profession of faith —

verses.name: I Timothy 6:14
verses.text: I implore you to keep his command free from stain or reproach, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:15
verses.text: This will be brought about in his own time by the one ever-blessed Potentate, the king of all kings and Lord of all lords,

verses.name: I Timothy 6:16
verses.text: who alone is possessed of immortality and dwells in unapproachable light, whom no one has ever seen or ever can see — to whom be ascribed honor and power for ever. Amen.  <div eID="gen8602" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 6:17
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1232"/><div sID="gen8603" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1232"/> Teach those who are wealthy in this life not to pride themselves, or fix their hopes, on so uncertain a thing as wealth, but on God, who gives us a wealth of enjoyment on every side.

verses.name: I Timothy 6:18
verses.text: Teach them to show kindness, to exhibit a wealth of good actions, to be open-handed and generous,

verses.name: I Timothy 6:19
verses.text: storing up for themselves what in the future will prove to be a good foundation, so that they may gain the only true life.  <div eID="gen8603" type="paragraph"/>

verses.name: I Timothy 6:20
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1233"/><div sID="gen8604" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1233"/> Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Avoid the profane prattle and contradictions of what some miscall ‘theology,’

verses.name: I Timothy 6:21
verses.text: for there are those who, while asserting their proficiency in it, have yet, as regards the faith, gone altogether astray. <div eID="gen8604" type="paragraph"/> <div sID="gen8605" type="section"/> <div sID="gen8606" type="paragraph"/> God bless you all.  <div eID="gen8606" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8605" type="section"/> <div eID="gen8601" type="majorSection"/> <chapter eID="1Tim.6"/> <div eID="gen8574" osisID="1Tim" type="book"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 1:1
verses.text: To Timothy, my dear child, from Paul who, by the will of God, is an apostle of Christ Jesus, charged to proclaim the life that comes from union with Christ Jesus. May God, the Father, and Christ Jesus, our Lord, bless you, and be merciful to you, and give you peace.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:3
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1234"/><div sID="gen8609" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1234"/> I am thankful to God, whom I serve, as my ancestors did, with a clear conscience, when I remember you, as I never fail to do, in my prayers — night and day alike,

verses.name: II Timothy 1:4
verses.text: as I think of your tears, longing to see you, that my happiness may be completed,

verses.name: II Timothy 1:5
verses.text: now that I have been reminded of the sincere faith that you have shown. That faith was seen first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and is now, I am convinced, in you also.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:6
verses.text: And that is my reason for reminding you to stir into flame that gift of God, which is yours through your ordination at my hands.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:7
verses.text: For the Spirit which God gave us was not a spirit of cowardice, but a spirit of power, love, and self-control.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:8
verses.text: Do not, therefore, be ashamed of the testimony which we have to bear to our Lord, or of me imprisoned for his sake; but join with me in suffering for the good news, as far as God enables you.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:9
verses.text: It was God who saved us, and from him we received our solemn call — not as a reward for anything that we had done, but in fulfillment of his own loving purpose. For that love was extended to us, through Christ Jesus, before time began,

verses.name: II Timothy 1:10
verses.text: and has now been made apparent through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus; who has made an end of death, and has brought life and Immortality to light by that good news,

verses.name: II Timothy 1:11
verses.text: of which I was myself appointed a herald and apostle, and teacher.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:12
verses.text: That is why I am undergoing these sufferings; yet I feel no shame, for I know in whom I have put my faith, and am convinced that he is able to guard what I have entrusted to him until ‘that day.’

verses.name: II Timothy 1:13
verses.text: Keep before you, as an example of sound teaching, all that you learnt from me as you listened with that faith and love which come from union with Christ Jesus.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:14
verses.text: Guard by the help of the Holy Spirit, who is within us, the glorious trust that has been committed to you.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:15
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1235"/><div sID="gen8610" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1235"/> You know, of course, that all our friends in Roman Asia turned their backs on me, and among them Phygellus and Hermogenes.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:16
verses.text: May the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus; for he often cheered me and was not ashamed of my chains.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:17
verses.text: On the contrary, when he arrived in Rome, he sought eagerly for me until he found me.

verses.name: II Timothy 1:18
verses.text: The Lord grant that he may find mercy at the hands of the Lord on ‘that day.’ The many services that he rendered at Ephesus you have the best means of knowing.  <div eID="gen8610" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8609" type="section"/> <chapter eID="2Tim.1"/> <div eID="gen8608" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 2:1
verses.text: You must, then, my child, find strength in the help which comes from the union with Christ Jesus;

verses.name: II Timothy 2:2
verses.text: and what you learnt from me, in the presence of many listeners, entrust to reliable people, who will be able in their turn to teach others.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:3
verses.text: Share hardships with me, as a true soldier of Christ Jesus.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:4
verses.text: A soldier on active service, to please his superior officer, always avoids entangling himself in the affairs of ordinary life.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:5
verses.text: No athlete is ever awarded the wreath of victory unless they have kept the rules.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:6
verses.text: The laborer who does the work should be the first to receive a share of the fruits of the earth.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:7
verses.text: Reflect on what I say; the Lord will always help you to understand.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:8
verses.text: Keep before your mind Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, a descendant of David, as told in the good news entrusted to me;

verses.name: II Timothy 2:9
verses.text: in the service of which I am suffering hardships, even to being put in fetters as a criminal. But the message of God is not fettered;

verses.name: II Timothy 2:10
verses.text: and that is why I submit to anything for the sake of God’s people: so that they also may obtain the salvation which comes from union with Christ Jesus, and imperishable glory.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:11
verses.text: How true this saying is — ‘If we have shared his death, we will also share his life.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:12
verses.text: If we continue to endure, we will also share his throne. If we should ever disown him, he, too, will disown us.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:13
verses.text: If we lose our trust, he is still to be trusted, for he cannot be false to himself!’

verses.name: II Timothy 2:14
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1236"/><div sID="gen8612" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1236"/> Remind people of all this; tell them solemnly, as in the sight of God, to avoid controversy, a useless thing and the ruin of those who listen to it.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:15
verses.text: Do your utmost to show yourself true to God, a worker with no reason to be ashamed, accurate in delivering the message of the truth.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:16
verses.text: Avoid profane prattle. Those who indulge in it only get deeper into irreligious ways,

verses.name: II Timothy 2:17
verses.text: and their teaching will spread like a cancer. Hymenaeus and Philetus are instances of this.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:18
verses.text: They have gone completely astray as regards the truth; they say that a resurrection has already taken place, and so upset some people’s faith.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:19
verses.text: Yet God’s firm foundation still stands unmoved, and it bears this inscription — <lg sID="gen8613"/> <l sID="gen8614"/>‘THE LORD KNOWS THOSE WHO ARE HIS’;<l eID="gen8614"/> <lg eID="gen8613"/> and this — <lg sID="gen8615"/> <l sID="gen8616"/>‘LET ALL THOSE WHO USE THE NAME OF THE LORD TURN AWAY FROM WICKEDNESS.’<l eID="gen8616"/> <lg eID="gen8615"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 2:20
verses.text: Now in a large house there are not only things of gold and silver, but also others of wood and earthenware, some for better and some for common use.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:21
verses.text: If, then, a person has escaped from the pollution of such errors as I have mentioned, they will be like a thing kept for better use, set apart, serviceable to its owner, ready for any good purpose.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:22
verses.text: Flee from the passions of youth, but pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, in the company of those who, with a pure heart, invoke the Lord.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:23
verses.text: Shun foolish and ignorant discussions, for you know that they only breed quarrels;

verses.name: II Timothy 2:24
verses.text: and a servant of the Lord should never quarrel. They ought, on the contrary, to be courteous to everyone, skillful teachers, and forbearing.

verses.name: II Timothy 2:25
verses.text: They should instruct their opponents in a gentle spirit; for, possibly, God may give those opponents a repentance that will lead to a fuller knowledge of truth,

verses.name: II Timothy 2:26
verses.text: and they may yet come to a sober mind, and escape from the devil's net, when captured by the Lord’s servant to do the will of God.  <div eID="gen8612" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="2Tim.2"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 3:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1237"/><div sID="gen8617" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1237"/> Be sure of this, that in the last days difficult times will come.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:2
verses.text: People will be selfish, mercenary, boastful, haughty, and blasphemous; disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, impure,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:3
verses.text: incapable of affection, merciless, slanderous, wanting in self-control, brutal, careless of the right,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:4
verses.text: treacherous, reckless, and puffed up with pride; they will love pleasure more than they love God;

verses.name: II Timothy 3:5
verses.text: and while they retain the outward form of religion, they will not allow it to influence them. Turn your back on such people as these.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:6
verses.text: For among them are to be found those who creep into homes and captivate weak women — women who, loaded with sins, and slaves to all kinds of passions,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:7
verses.text: are always learning, and yet never able to attain to a real knowledge of the truth.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:8
verses.text: Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so do these people, in their turn, oppose the truth. Their minds are corrupted, and, as regards the faith, they are utterly worthless.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:9
verses.text: They will not, however, make further progress; for their wicked folly will be plain to everyone, just as the folly Jannes and Jambres was.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:10
verses.text: But you, Timothy, were a close observer of my teaching, my conduct, my purposes, my faith, my forbearance, my love, and my patient endurance,

verses.name: II Timothy 3:11
verses.text: as well as of my persecutions, and of the sufferings which I met with at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. You know what persecutions I underwent; and yet the Lord brought me safe out of all!

verses.name: II Timothy 3:12
verses.text: Yes, and all who aim at living a religious life in union with Christ Jesus will have to suffer persecution;

verses.name: II Timothy 3:13
verses.text: but wicked people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving others and deceived themselves.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:14
verses.text: You, however, must stand by what you learnt and accepted as true. You know who they were from whom you learnt it;

verses.name: II Timothy 3:15
verses.text: and that, from your childhood, you have known the sacred writings, which can give you the wisdom that, through belief in Christ Jesus, leads to salvation.

verses.name: II Timothy 3:16
verses.text: All scripture is God-breathed: helpful for teaching, for refuting error, for giving guidance, and for training others in righteousness;

verses.name: II Timothy 3:17
verses.text: so that God’s people may be capable and equipped for good work of every kind.  <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1238"/><div sID="gen8618" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8618" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="2Tim.3"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 4:1
verses.text: I solemnly charge you, in the sight of God and of Christ Jesus, who will one day judge the living and the dead — I charge you by his appearing and by his kingdom: —

verses.name: II Timothy 4:2
verses.text: Proclaim the message, be ready in season and out of season, convince, rebuke, encourage, never failing to instruct with forbearance.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:3
verses.text: For a time will come when people will not tolerate sound teaching. They will follow their own wishes, and, in their itching for novelty, procure themselves a crowd of teachers.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:4
verses.text: They will turn a deaf ear to the truth, and give their attention to legends instead.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:5
verses.text: But you, Timothy, must always be temperate. Face hardships; do the work of a missionary; discharge all the duties of your office.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:6
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1238"/><div sID="gen8619" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1238"/> As for me, my life blood is already being poured out; the time of my departure is close at hand.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:7
verses.text: I have run the great race; I have finished the course; I have kept the faith.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:8
verses.text: And now the crown of righteousness awaits me, which the Lord, the just judge, will give me on ‘that day’ — and not only to me, but to all who have loved his appearing.  <div eID="gen8619" type="paragraph"/> <div eID="gen8617" type="section"/> <div eID="gen8611" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 4:9
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1239"/><div sID="gen8620" type="majorSection"/> <title>Conclusion</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1239"/> Do your utmost to come to me soon;

verses.name: II Timothy 4:10
verses.text: for Demas, in his love for the world, has deserted me. He has gone to Thessalonica, Crescens to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:11
verses.text: There is no one but Luke with me. Pick up Mark on your way, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me in my work.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:12
verses.text: I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:13
verses.text: Bring with you, when you come, the cloak which I left at Troas with Carpus, and the books, especially the parchments.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:14
verses.text: Alexander, the coppersmith, showed much ill feeling towards me. ‘The Lord will give him what his actions deserve.’

verses.name: II Timothy 4:15
verses.text: You must also on your guard against him, for he is strongly opposed to our teaching.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:16
verses.text: At my first trial no one stood by me. They all deserted me. May it never be counted against them!

verses.name: II Timothy 4:17
verses.text: But the Lord came to my help and strengthened me, in order that, through me, the proclamation should be made so widely that all the Gentiles should hear it; and I was rescued ‘out of the Lion’s mouth.’

verses.name: II Timothy 4:18
verses.text: The Lord will rescue me from all evil, and bring me safe into his Heavenly kingdom. All glory to him for ever and ever! Amen.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:19
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1240"/><div sID="gen8621" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1240"/> Give my greeting to Prisca and Aquila, and to the household of Onesiphorus.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:20
verses.text: Erastus remained at Corinth, and I left Thophimus ill at Miletus.

verses.name: II Timothy 4:21
verses.text: Do your utmost to come before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus and Claudia send you their greetings, and so do the rest of the Lord's followers.  <div eID="gen8621" type="section"/>

verses.name: II Timothy 4:22
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1241"/><div sID="gen8622" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1241"/> May the Lord be with your soul. God bless you all.  <div eID="gen8622" type="section"/> <div eID="gen8620" type="majorSection"/> <chapter eID="2Tim.4"/> <div eID="gen8607" osisID="2Tim" type="book"/>

verses.name: Titus 1:1
verses.text: From Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, charged to strengthen the faith of God’s chosen people, and their knowledge of that truth which makes for godliness

verses.name: Titus 1:2
verses.text: and is based on the hope of eternal life, which God, who never lies, promised before the ages began,

verses.name: Titus 1:3
verses.text: and has revealed at his own time in his message, with the proclamation of which I was entrusted by the command of God our Savior.

verses.name: Titus 1:4
verses.text: To Titus, my true child in our one faith: May God, the Father, and Christ Jesus, our Savior, bless you and give you peace.  <div eID="gen8624" type="majorSection"/>

verses.name: Titus 1:5
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1242"/><div sID="gen8625" type="majorSection"/> <title>Mission of Titus in Crete</title> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1242"/> My reason for leaving you in Crete was that you might put in order what had been left unsettled, and appoint officers of the church in the various towns, as I myself directed you.

verses.name: Titus 1:6
verses.text: They are to be of irreproachable character, faithful to their partners, whose children are Christians and have never been charged with dissolute conduct or have been unruly.

verses.name: Titus 1:7
verses.text: For a presiding officer, as God’s steward, ought to be of irreproachable character; not self-willed or quick-tempered, nor addicted to drink or to brawling or to questionable money-making.

verses.name: Titus 1:8
verses.text: On the contrary, they should be hospitable, eager for the right, discreet, upright, people of holy life and capable of self-restraint,

verses.name: Titus 1:9
verses.text: who hold doctrine that can be relied on as being in accordance with the accepted teaching; so that they may be able to encourage others by sound teaching, as well as to refute our opponents.

verses.name: Titus 1:10
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1243"/><div sID="gen8626" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1243"/> There are, indeed, many unruly persons — great talkers who deceive themselves, principally converts from Judaism,

verses.name: Titus 1:11
verses.text: whose mouths ought to be stopped; for they upset whole households by teaching what they ought not to teach, merely to make questionable gains.

verses.name: Titus 1:12
verses.text: It was a Cretan — one of their own teachers — who said: ‘Cretans are always liars, base brutes, and gluttonous idlers’; and his statement is true.

verses.name: Titus 1:13
verses.text: Therefore rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith,

verses.name: Titus 1:14
verses.text: and may pay no attention to Jewish legends, or to the directions of those who turn their backs on the truth.

verses.name: Titus 1:15
verses.text: Everything is pure to the pure-minded, but to those whose minds are polluted and who are unbelievers nothing is pure. Their minds and consciences are alike polluted.

verses.name: Titus 1:16
verses.text: They profess to know God, but by their actions they disown him. They are degraded and self-willed; and, as far as anything good is concerned, they are utterly worthless.  <div eID="gen8626" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Titus.1"/>

verses.name: Titus 2:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1244"/><div sID="gen8627" type="section"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1244"/> You should, however, speak of such subjects as properly have a place in sound Christian teaching.

verses.name: Titus 2:2
verses.text: Teach that the older men should be temperate, serious, and discreet; strong in faith, love, and endurance.

verses.name: Titus 2:3
verses.text: So, too, that the older women should be reverent in their demeanor, and that they should avoid scandal, and beware of becoming slaves to drink;

verses.name: Titus 2:4
verses.text: that they should teach what is right, so as to train the younger women to love their husbands and children,

verses.name: Titus 2:5
verses.text: and to be discreet, pure-minded, domesticated, good women, respecting the authority of their husbands, in order that God’s message may not be maligned.

verses.name: Titus 2:6
verses.text: And so again with the younger men — impress on them the need of discretion.

verses.name: Titus 2:7
verses.text: Above all, set an example of doing good. Show sincerity in your teaching, and a serious spirit;

verses.name: Titus 2:8
verses.text: let the instruction that you give be sound and above reproach, so that the enemy may be ashamed when he fails to find anything bad to say about us.

verses.name: Titus 2:9
verses.text: Tell slaves to respect their owner's authority in all circumstances, and to try their best to please them.

verses.name: Titus 2:10
verses.text: Teach them not to contradict or to pilfer, but to show such praiseworthy fidelity in everything, as to recommend the teaching about God our Savior by all that they do.

verses.name: Titus 2:11
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1245"/><div sID="gen8628" type="paragraph"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1245"/> For the loving kindness of God has been revealed, bringing salvation for all;

verses.name: Titus 2:12
verses.text: leading us to renounce irreligious ways and worldly ambitions, and to live discreet, upright, and religious lives here in this present world,

verses.name: Titus 2:13
verses.text: while we are awaiting our blessed hope — the appearing in glory of our great God and Savior, Christ Jesus.

verses.name: Titus 2:14
verses.text: For he gave himself on our behalf, to deliver us from all wickedness, and to purify for himself a people who should be peculiarly his own and eager to do good.

verses.name: Titus 2:15
verses.text: Speak of all this, and encourage and rebuke with all authority. Do not let anyone despise you.  <div eID="gen8628" type="paragraph"/> <chapter eID="Titus.2"/>

verses.name: Titus 3:1
verses.text: Remind your hearers to respect and obey the powers that be, to be ready for every kind of good work, to speak ill of no one, to avoid quarreling,

verses.name: Titus 3:2
verses.text: to be forbearing, and under all circumstances to show a gentle spirit in dealing with others, whoever they may be.

verses.name: Titus 3:3
verses.text: There was, you remember, a time when we ourselves were foolish, disobedient, misled, slaves to all kinds of passions and vices, living in a spirit of malice and envy, detested ourselves and hating one another.

verses.name: Titus 3:4
verses.text: But, when the kindness of God our Savior and his love for humanity were revealed, he saved us,

verses.name: Titus 3:5
verses.text: not as the result of any righteous actions that we had done, but in fulfillment of his merciful purposes. He saved us by that washing which was a new birth to us, and by the renewing power of the Holy Spirit,

verses.name: Titus 3:6
verses.text: which he poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior;

verses.name: Titus 3:7
verses.text: that, having been pronounced righteous through his loving kindness, we might enter on our inheritance with the hope of eternal life.

verses.name: Titus 3:8
verses.text: How true that saying is! And it is on these subjects that I desire you to lay especial stress, so that those who have learned to trust in God may be careful to devote themselves to doing good. Such subjects are excellent in themselves, and of real use to humanity.

verses.name: Titus 3:9
